## 012 — Less reading, more plumbing

**Date:** October 13, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)

**Build:** Prototype 12 / 0.12.0 / Godot 4.7.2 / standalone macOS app

The title keeps its artwork and logo, with only Start, Controls, and Quit. Original keyboard and generic
Xbox-compatible gamepad diagrams explain every assigned action in one dedicated screen with two pages.
Button hints elsewhere and the tutorial are removed. Selecting an employee starts the basement immediately.

![Simplified title](012-clean-title-and-controls/01-title.jpg)

![Keyboard reference](012-clean-title-and-controls/02-keyboard.jpg)

![Gamepad reference](012-clean-title-and-controls/03-gamepad.jpg)

![Immediate basement gameplay](012-clean-title-and-controls/04-basement.jpg)

Six automated suites pass: movement/combat, crew, dialogue, basement progression, title navigation, and sprite
alignment. macOS export and signature verification pass. Screens were checked in a small agent-only window.
The basement still contains three toilets. Expanded encounters, acid hazards, and the Clogfather await Storyboarding.
No new physical-controller playtest was requested. Markdown lint tooling is unavailable; whitespace was checked.

Twelve SNES opening/title images were inspected in the
[reference collection](https://www.fandomspot.com/snes-best-title-screens/): F-Zero, Plok, Super Tennis,
Battletoads in Battlemaniacs, Pilotwings, The Lost Vikings, Mortal Kombat II, Mega Man X, Super Mario Kart,
Star Fox, A Link to the Past, and Super Mario World. Most show a logo, artwork, copyright, and at most a short
prompt or small menu. Some captures precede the menu animation. None provide a full control guide.
Reference artwork was not imported into the game.

## 013 — First names only

**Date:** October 13, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)

**Build:** Prototype 13 / 0.12.1 / Godot 4.7.2 / standalone macOS app

Selection cards and dialogue now use Tony and Sean only. The separate full-name field was removed so both
screens use the same first-name source. This convention is recorded in the project instructions.

**Capture gap:** Screenshots await permission for a visual session. The game was not opened or foregrounded.
Earlier screenshots remain historical records. Preserve this build until selection and gameplay captures can be added.

## 014 — Metadata-driven combat and visible damage

**Date:** October 13, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)

**Build:** Prototype 14 / 0.14.0 / Godot 4.7.2 / standalone macOS app

Canonical per-weapon and per-monster JSON now generates a validated exportable runtime bundle. Tony's pressure gun
uses 6 damage every 0.15 seconds and a 500-pixel range. Sean's plunger uses 40 damage every second
and a 650-pixel range.
Flushfiends have 40 HP. Player health and movement remain unchanged while the proposed player balance is unresolved.

Every hit flashes and emits particles, even without crossing a damage threshold. Five living damage stages lead to
a nonlooping four-frame death. Remains fall to the floor and hold the last frame. Health bars are continuous and hidden
by default, with a session-only toggle in Controls. Source artwork is preserved; runtime alpha cutoff and measured
Flushfiend row crops prevent haze and neighboring-row bleed. All poses share a scale rather than resizing individually.

Sean explicitly approved this small-window visual session. The preview and exported gameplay were inspected and closed.

![Six damage stages at two scales](014-metadata-and-damage/01-damage-preview.jpg)

![Optional health bars in Controls](014-metadata-and-damage/02-health-bar-option.jpg)

![First-name-only employee selection and updated cadence](014-metadata-and-damage/03-selection.jpg)

![Damaged Flushfiend during actual gameplay](014-metadata-and-damage/04-damaged-flushfiend.jpg)

![Grounded rubble with health bars hidden](014-metadata-and-damage/05-settled-rubble.jpg)

Seven Godot regression suites and three Python validation tests pass. Checks cover ownership and unsupported weapons,
missing IDs, invalid types/ranges, exact HP boundaries, repeated hits, death completion, reset, swept collisions,
solid platforms, travel-distance limits, and atlas loading. Export/signature checks pass; the exported package was
checked from outside the source directory to verify runtime JSON inclusion and marketing-art exclusion.
Deliberate invalid-ID/ownership cases log errors. Headless combat/crew tests also report an AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback
shutdown reference warning; assertions pass, and no gameplay crash was observed. Markdown lint tooling is unavailable;
changed documents were checked for whitespace and line width.

Still pending: four additional weapon mechanics, loadout UI, new weapon-art attachment, Widow flight gameplay, and
further small-scale readability polish. The Widow's 80 HP and damage/death animations are preview-only; wing gutters
and thorax alignment remain provisional. Boss gameplay and expanded basement flow are separate work.
Prototype 13 remains preserved in `builds/history/Prototype-13.app` for its deferred historical captures.

## 015 — Opening-screen music

**Date:** October 14, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)

**Build:** Prototype 15 / 0.15.0 / Godot 4.7.2

The brief from Storyboarding calls for cheerful professional confidence with trouble underneath: energetic retro
rhythm, warmth for Tony and Sean, and playful instrumentation. The first stock cue is “Face The Facts” by Zane Little
Music, released under CC0. It replaces the short synthesized sting and repeats throughout the opening menus and
employee selection. Gameplay stops it; returning to the title restarts it unless muted.

The source WAV, license/source metadata, adaptation recipe, and earlier sting code are preserved in `audio/`.
The full cue retains its ending before repeating; it is not a verified seamless musical loop. Custom character motifs,
level and boss music, voice acting, and subjective listening approval remain pending.

Headless title lifecycle tests pass, including repeat configuration, mute, gameplay stop, and return playback.
Audio decodes successfully with a measured peak of -1 dBFS. macOS export and signature verification pass.
Godot reports sandbox-related certificate, log, and editor-settings warnings. Markdown lint is unavailable;
changed prose received whitespace and width checks.

**Capture gap:** No game window was opened because this request did not authorize a foreground playtest.
Title and representative gameplay screenshots remain pending in `015-title-music/`; no earlier images were reused.
The exported Prototype 15 build is preserved in `builds/history/Prototype-15.app` for later capture.

## 016 — Hero at the door, Hallow in the basement

**Date:** October 14, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)

**Build:** Prototype 16 / 0.16.0 / Godot 4.7.2 / standalone macOS app

Sean's chosen songs now accompany the opening and first level: “It Takes A Hero” and “Hallow Quest” (16-bit),
both by Zane Little Music (CC0). A single music voice fades between tracks. Hero plays its full ending before
repeating; Hallow uses its authored loop. Music mute follows the player, pause suspends playback, restart continues
level music, and return-to-title restores Hero. Dialogue reduces the music level. Effects remain independent.

**October 14 capture follow-up:** Sean explicitly approved a small preview. Original window-only captures now show
Prototype 16's title and basement, plus the current development damage preview. The preview shows airborne death
fragments and settled remains for both creatures. Living stages remain within their columns; Widow anchors remain
provisional. These still images do not validate the brief hit flash in motion. No new boss encounter is shown.
Both preview and game windows were closed afterward. No player interaction was requested.

Prototype 16 is preserved in `builds/history/Prototype-16.zip`; Prototype 15 also remains archived.

Headless checks cover track identity/duration, gain, fade sequencing, mute, pause, restart, return, title repeat,
rapid transition cancellation, and cleanup. Source and runtime hashes match the Audio handoff.
Export inclusion is checked from outside the project directory. Subjective listening remains pending.

## 020 — A field guide with fingerprints

**Date:** October 14, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)

**Build:** Prototype 20 / 0.20.1 / Godot 4.7.2 / standalone macOS app

The Controls pages now use original worn keyboard and rounded, unbranded controller illustrations with grime,
rust and plumber's tape. Four prominent action cards sit beside the hardware. Smaller job, menu, and conversation
cards replace the old wall of mixed-device instructions. Music and enemy-bar settings have separate clickable
footer buttons. Existing gameplay mappings remain unchanged.

Reference research used the Alien: Isolation manual and EA's F1 25 keyboard guide for diagram/legend structure.
No artwork from those sources was copied. Exact prompts, source links, and image dimensions are preserved in
`assets/controls/art-v1.json`; the unused second controller variation is retained alongside the selected original.

**Validation:** Headless tests cover primary label widths, texture dimensions, separate setting hit areas,
and keyboard/controller navigation and toggles. Menu regression checks pass. Existing intermittent Godot
headless cleanup warnings may occur after passing assertions. Markdown lint is unavailable; text hygiene checked.

**Approved visual review:** Sean authorized a small preview. Both Controls pages were checked for readable text,

menu audio. Scripted movement uses invulnerability and does not establish survival balance. Existing environment
and shutdown-resource warnings remain; no script errors occurred in the passing suites.

## 048 — Employees behind glass — October 16, 2026

**Build:** Prototype 48 / 0.48.0.

The missing glass-front dispenser handoff is integrated. Art supplied cabinet, glass and hatch layers around two
sleeping copies of the selected hero. Each occupant is clipped to its own compartment and animates with the gameplay
clock. Existing checkpoint healing, hand/impact gag, emergence and respawn timings remain unchanged; no stock or
restocking mechanic is added. All earlier art remains preserved.

BJ’s dialogue role label now matches his established title. Story reviewed the current dialogue and kept the approved
lines intact. Widow backstory now matches the approved shared lore; this adds no reproduction behavior. The audit
confirmed that the full-route wastewater cutaway and server-rack BJ were already integrated. Marketing portraits
remain marketing assets.

**Validation:** Export/signing, nine Python tests and six packaged suites pass: glass stock/geometry, dispenser
lifecycle, dialogue, completion, wastewater and integrated level. BJ’s longest role label measures 376 of 520 available
pixels. Live composition remains pending. Existing environment and shutdown-resource warnings persist; no script
errors occurred in the passing checks.

**Capture gap:** No game window opened. Preserve `builds/history/Prototype-48.zip` for actual screenshots after
permission. Source-art inspection and geometry checks do not substitute for running-game screenshots.

## 049 — A swoop, steady feet, and clearer platforms — October 16, 2026

**Build:** Prototype 49 / 0.49.0.

The enlarged 180-HP Widow now warns before committing to a captured target position, swoops into the player lane,
and recovers before another attack. Scenery stops its expanded body; the attack does not home after commitment.
Art and Level replaced all twenty raised surfaces with moss-green frames and lighter treads across four families,
preserving geometry. The optional new Widow lunge pose awaits visual registration; current flight art is retained.

Sean’s clone shifted almost a sprite width when looking left because the renderer treated a negative width as a UV
flip, while our code also shifted its left edge. Mirroring now respects the frame anchor, with checks for both heroes,
both facings and emergence/look/shrug poses. The behavior is confirmed in
[Godot’s canvas renderer](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_cull.cpp).

Both endings now contain nine reciprocal turns with emotional portraits. Headless tests confirm support-radio lines,
typewriter reveal, held-input behavior and the final release guard. The old source already included Sean’s response;
the reported missing turn was not reproduced, so a separate runtime omission is not claimed fixed.

**Validation:** Export/signing, nine Python tests and ten packaged suites pass: durable flyer, dispenser registration,
ending input, completion, dispenser lifecycle, glass stock, integrated traversal, standing shots, running shots and
platform geometry. Existing environment and shutdown-resource warnings persist; no script errors occurred.

**Capture gap:** Daughter’s active playtest remains untouched. No game window opened. The new app will be delivered
separately at `builds/Prototype-49/Drain Damage.app`, preserving the existing default app. Actual screenshots and
human swoop/contrast/animation review await permission; archive `builds/history/Prototype-49.zip` for later capture.

## 050 — Wreckage that stays, preparation before play — October 16, 2026

**Build:** Prototype 50 / 0.50.0.

Sean reported opening Flushfiends disappearing on defeat and a one-time midair freeze near the start. The opening
adapter removed defeated actors after 0.6 seconds, bypassing the later level’s persistent wreckage. Opening runners
now enter the shared corpse list with their position, direction and death animation; cleanup removes only the actor.
Kill credit and shatter sound remain single events. Restart clears wreckage as before.

The first drawn Flushfiend also performed a synchronous pixel-by-pixel damage-atlas cleanup. A headless measurement
found about 237 ms cold versus 0.003 ms cached. Preparation now occurs before gameplay; shared textures and frame data
are reused across restarts and new games. This removes a measured stall source but is not a live confirmation that all
of the reported hitch is gone. GPU first-use behavior is outside headless validation.

**Validation:** Export/signing, nine Python tests and nine packaged suites pass, including both heroes and runner
roles, death-frame progression, retained wreckage beyond four seconds, single kill/audio, reset cleanup, cache reuse,
continuous level traversal, standing/running shots, swoop, pause, completion and title lifecycle. Existing environment
and shutdown-resource warnings remain; no script errors occurred in the passing suites.

**Capture gap:** No game opened or foregrounded. Separate app `builds/Prototype-50/Drain Damage.app` and archive
`builds/history/Prototype-50.zip` preserve this iteration for actual screenshots after permission. Earlier builds and
captures remain intact.

Prototype 50 was rebuilt on request October 16 at `builds/Drain Damage.app`. Signing and the packaged
opening-wreckage/warmup regression check passed. No new visual iteration or screenshot is claimed.

## 051 — One checkpoint and one spare — October 16, 2026

**Build:** Prototype 51 / 0.51.0.

Sean reduced the first level to one checkpoint near the midpoint. Level chose x4650, roughly 49% of the route, to keep
the cabinet clear of the next platform. Extra machines and triggers are gone. Art approved using the existing left
compartment for one sleeping copy of the selected hero and leaving the right compartment empty.

Full-health check-in saves progress without consuming stock. The first replacement consumes the clone when vending
begins; skipping the replacement completes that same single use. Afterward, the cabinet remains empty across deaths
and revisits. Subsequent respawns arrive beside it with no duplicate vending, emerging clone or invented refill.
A new run restores stock. Checkpoint activation and stock are independent; the existing three lives remain unchanged.

**Validation:** Export/signing, nine Python tests and eight packaged suites pass: dispenser lifecycle/stock, glass
slots, integrated traversal, midpoint recovery, clone registration, opening wreckage/warmup, ending input and pause.

`builds/history/Prototype-51.zip` preserve this iteration for actual screenshots after permission. Earlier apps remain.

## 052 — A flush for the fallen — October 16, 2026

**Build:** Prototype 52 / 0.52.0.

Audio delivered a three-second CC0 toilet-flush recording with preserved source and processing provenance. It plays
once on either hero’s actual death transition, including the final life, replacing the short lethal-hit tone. Ordinary
hits, enemy deaths and the dispenser gag do not trigger it. Manual pause suspends playback; the automatic death popup
and respawn allow it to finish naturally. Title, new run and shutdown clean it up. Audio never gates gameplay timing.

**Validation:** Export/signing, nine Python tests and six packaged suites pass: hero death audio, dispenser,
Flushfiend shatter, pause, completion and integrated level. Natural audio completion is tested with allowance for

Existing environment and shutdown-resource warnings remain; no script errors occurred in the passing checks.

## 053 — Swarms with substance and forward swoops — October 16, 2026

**Build:** Prototype 53 / 0.53.0.

Septic Air Force now uses a 48-pixel contact radius instead of 16, covering most of the visible fly mass.
The same shared bounds apply to shots and scenery. The Hallowed Widow maintains its heading through a V-shaped
attack, climbing forward to its original altitude rather than retracing the dive. It flies straight during cooldown;
obstacles still stop unsafe movement.

The title and gameplay now show a small white-on-dark version badge at the lower right, inset 16 pixels.

and the Makefile synchronizes macOS bundle versions before export. Future release handoffs, platform blockers,
installation/testing evidence, and requested LFS package storage are documented in the project README.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Drain Damage — The road to a real game</title>
<style>
:root { color-scheme: dark; --bg:#101c2a; --panel:#192b3b; --line:#334957; --text:#eef4ed;
  --muted:#b3c3cb; --mint:#7ce4bc; --gold:#ffcf70; }
* { box-sizing:border-box; }
body { margin:0; background:var(--bg); color:var(--text); font:16px/1.6 system-ui,sans-serif; }
a { color:var(--mint); text-underline-offset:4px; }
a:hover { color:white; }
.wrap { max-width:1140px; margin:auto; padding:40px 28px 70px; }
.kicker { font:700 12px/1.5 ui-monospace,monospace; letter-spacing:2px; color:var(--mint); }
header { padding:24px 0 32px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); }
h1 { font-size:clamp(38px,6vw,68px); line-height:1.05; letter-spacing:-2px; margin:20px 0; max-width:850px; }
.intro { font-size:20px; max-width:780px; color:var(--muted); }
.meta { font-size:13px; color:var(--muted); }
.summary { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr); gap:16px; margin:26px 0; }
.summary article { border-left:3px solid var(--mint); padding:12px 18px; background:var(--panel); }
.summary strong { display:block; font-size:21px; }
.summary span { font-size:14px; color:var(--muted); }
figure { margin:28px 0; }
figure img { width:100%; max-width:740px; display:block; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:12px; }
figcaption { color:var(--muted); font-size:13px; margin-top:8px; }
nav { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px; margin:28px 0 10px; }
button { font:inherit; font-size:14px; color:var(--text); background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius:30px; padding:8px 18px; cursor:pointer; }
button[aria-pressed="true"] { color:var(--bg); background:var(--mint); border-color:var(--mint); }
button:focus-visible, a:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--gold); outline-offset:4px; }
.phase { margin:22px 0; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:14px; overflow:hidden; background:var(--panel); }
.phase-head { display:flex; gap:22px; padding:26px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); }
.number { font:700 28px ui-monospace,monospace; color:var(--mint); min-width:45px; padding-top:6px; }
h2 { font-size:27px; line-height:1.2; margin:8px 0; letter-spacing:-.5px; }
.phase-head p { margin:0; color:var(--muted); font-size:14px; }
.badge { text-transform:uppercase; font-size:11px; letter-spacing:1.5px; color:var(--muted); font-weight:750; }
.done { color:var(--mint); } .next { color:var(--gold); } .research { color:#b6b2ff; }
.tasks { list-style:none; padding:0; margin:0; display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; }
.tasks li { padding:20px 26px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); }
h3 { margin:0 0 6px; font-size:17px; }
.tasks p { margin:0; color:var(--muted); font-size:15px; }
.gate { padding:18px 26px; margin:0; font-size:14px; color:var(--gold); }
.notes { padding:26px; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:14px; margin-top:26px; }
.notes p, .notes li { color:var(--muted); }
.notes h2 { font-size:23px; }
footer { margin-top:32px; color:var(--muted); font-size:13px; }
[hidden] { display:none !important; }
@media(max-width:650px) { .wrap { padding:20px 16px 45px; } .summary,.tasks { grid-template-columns:1fr; }
  .phase-head { padding:20px; gap:12px; } h2 { font-size:24px; } .tasks li { padding:18px 20px; } }
@media print { :root { color-scheme:light; --bg:white; --panel:white; --text:#172432; --muted:#354653;
  --line:#bcc6cc; --mint:#146047; --gold:#77520c; } nav,.filter-note { display:none; }
  .phase[hidden] { display:block !important; } .phase-head,.tasks li { break-inside:avoid; }
  .wrap { padding:0; } h1 { font-size:40px; } a { color:#146047; } }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<main class="wrap">
<header>
<div class="kicker">DRAIN DAMAGE / DEVELOPMENT ROADMAP</div>
<h1>From three angry toilets<br>to a real adventure.</h1>
<p>Build delivery policy: integrated game changes receive a new build and a readiness update with the version,
changes and remaining testing gaps. Builds may wait for related agent deliveries; pending work will be stated explicitly.
Opening the game still requires Sean’s permission.</p>
<p><strong>Platform palette revision:</strong> Beige foreground platforms rejected in playtest. <a href="assets/world/opening-trial/moss-platform-scene-mockup-v1.png">Oxidized moss-green scene mockup</a> applies consistent readable landing edges to small plinths and large pump platforms. Integrated across all 20 raised surfaces in Prototype 49; live contrast review pending.</p>
<p><strong>Marketing hero portraits:</strong> Hyperrealistic Tony and Sean portraits derived only from illustrated designs replace the crew-profile references in editable magazine source. <a href="handoffs/hero-hyperreal-marketing-portraits.json">Art handoff</a>. Published PDF regeneration pending; game assets unchanged.</p>
<p><strong>Weapon roster art:</strong> <a href="weapons/roster-mockup/weapon-roster-v1.png">Labeled sprite-sheet mockup</a> covers six catalog weapons and seven concepts, with melee/short-range/long-range labels and playable/catalog/idea status. Proposed ranges remain provisional; no new weapons implemented. <a href="weapons/roster-mockup/roster-v1.json">Roster notes</a>.</p>
<p><a href="design/game-design-glossary.html">Game design glossary</a> — our shared terms for enemy roles, fair combat, level flow and balance.</p>
<p class="intro">A solo plumbing action game starring Sean and Tony.
Bright retro pixels. Adult humor. Forgiving action. One playable milestone at a time.</p>
<p class="meta">Updated October 16, 2026 · Current build: Prototype 55 / 0.55.0 · Primary target: Apple Silicon macOS</p>
<p>October 16: Prototype 50 rebuilt on request at builds/Drain Damage.app; signing and packaged opening-wreckage/warmup regression check passed. No game window opened.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 55 — selected app icon:</strong> Art’s porcelain-jaw/plunger design is integrated into the project and macOS app. Standard and Retina icon sizes are packaged into ICNS; exported bytes and version checks pass. Finder/Dock review and storybook screenshots await permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 54 — visible build version:</strong> A small high-contrast version badge now appears at the lower right of the title and gameplay screens. Project version is canonical and synchronized into macOS export metadata. Future explicit releases use coordinated readiness checks, platform-specific evidence, and Git LFS release packages; only macOS is currently supported. No multi-platform release is published. Visual review awaits permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 53 — swarm contact and Widow flight:</strong> Septic Air Force contact radius now matches most of its visible mass (48 pixels). The Widow climbs forward to its original altitude after a dive, maintaining heading and straight flight between attacks. Scenery collision remains enforced. Four packaged suites and nine Python tests pass; visual review and screenshots await permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 52 — hero death flush:</strong> Audio’s three-second toilet flush plays once when Tony or
Sean enters the dying state, including the final life. It replaces the short lethal-hit tone and does not play for
ordinary hits, Flushfiend defeats or the dispenser gag. Manual pause suspends it; the automatic death popup and
respawn let it finish naturally. Title/new-run/shutdown stop it. Gameplay timing does not wait on audio. Export/signing, nine Python tests and six packaged suites pass; listening and running screenshots remain pending. Separate build under builds/Prototype-52.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 51 — one midpoint checkpoint, one spare:</strong> The first level now has one checkpoint at
x4650, roughly 49% along the route on clear floor. Its cabinet holds one selected-hero clone in the left bay. Full-health
check-in leaves stock available; the first replacement consumes it. Later checkpoint respawns arrive beside the empty
cabinet without repeated vending or refilling. Empty stock persists through death/revisit and resets on a new run.
Three lives remain unchanged. Export/signing, nine Python tests and eight packaged suites pass; actual composition and screenshots await permission.
The separate app under builds/Prototype-51 preserves earlier apps and running playtests.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 50 — opening wreckage and first-appearance hitch:</strong> Defeated opening Flushfiends now
use the same persistent animated wreckage as later enemies, rather than disappearing after 0.6 seconds. Death sound
and kill credit occur once. The damage atlas is prepared before gameplay and shared across runs; first drawing no
longer scans every image pixel. A headless cold measurement was about 237 ms versus 0.003 ms cached. This removes a
measured source of stalls; live confirmation of the reported early jump hitch remains pending. Export/signing, nine Python tests and nine packaged suites pass.
The app is separate under builds/Prototype-50; no running playtest is interrupted.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 49 — swooping Widow and readable platforms:</strong> The 180-HP enlarged Widow warns for
0.65 seconds, commits to its captured target, and recovers after its dive; scenery stops its expanded body.
All 20 raised surfaces across four families now use Art’s moss-green frames and lighter treads without geometry
changes. Clone look-direction rendering preserves the feet anchor instead of shifting Sean sideways. Both endings
now have nine reciprocal turns; held-input tests retain every radio response. The old missing reply was not reproduced.
Export/signing, nine Python tests and ten packaged suites pass. Optional lunge-pose registration and live visual review remain
pending. Build 49 is delivered separately under builds/Prototype-49 to preserve the active family playtest’s app.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 48 — glass-front employee stock:</strong> Art’s new cabinet, glass and lower hatch layers
replace the old dispenser facade. Two sleeping copies of the selected hero occupy separate clipped compartments;
the existing checkpoint, hand, impact and emergence sequence remains intact. BJ’s dialogue role label now matches
his established title. Widow shared lore is synchronized with approved copy, without reproduction mechanics.
The audit confirms the full-route wastewater cutaway and server-rack BJ were already integrated. Export/signing, nine Python tests and six packaged suites pass; live composition and screenshots await permission. Marketing portraits remain outside the game.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 47 — open-route crowds and tougher flying spiders:</strong> Kill-count shutters are removed
from the first level. Four finite later waves contain 8, 10, 10 and 8 Flushfiends; entries remain offscreen, spaced and
bounded to eight live threats, reduced to six with a large flying spider. Checkpoints and physical scenery remain;
bypassed enemies do not grant kills. The temporary exit no longer requires clearing ordinary enemies. The playable
Clogfather is still pending. Hallowed Widow is twice its previous linear size with matching body targeting, 180 HP
and a fixed four-second hover before continuing its flight. First-level weapons take 15 Tony hits or 10 Sean hits.
Flushfiend lethal hits now use the supplied ceramic-style shatter, including environmental defeats; ordinary hits
retain their feedback. Four bounded audio voices honor pause, mute and cleanup. Export/signing, nine Python tests and nine packaged suites pass;
human crowd balance, enlarged-art readability and listening review remain pending. No game window opened.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 46 — wrench-clink navigation:</strong> Sean’s selected 0.24-second Kenney CC0 cue plays
once when directional keyboard, D-pad or stick navigation changes the main-menu focus, employee or controls page.
Ineffective directions, key echoes and repeated held D-pad/stick input stay silent. One voice prevents stacking;
gameplay and exit stop it. Existing SFX/Master mute is honored independently of the music toggle. Packaged navigation,
selection, controls and music checks pass; listening/mix review remains pending. No game window opened.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 45 — the faster opening is part of level one:</strong> Start now enters the continuous
9,600-pixel first level. The separate Opening Trial menu, timer cutoff and results popup are removed. The first two rooms
use sewer platforms and mixed enemy roles, with spatial entry triggers and safety checks; play continues into the later
rooms, checkpoints, shutters and exit without a reset. Starter weapons retain the faster profile throughout the level.
Art’s ivory frames and lighter steel pipe surfaces make solid plinths and deck tops stand apart from the dark wall.
Tony’s stationary horizontal shots now target the Flushfiend’s visible 43-pixel body rather than its shorter movement
collider. Both facings, both heroes and moving targets have regression coverage; high shots still miss.
Nine Python tests and ten packaged suites pass, including continuous 30-second movement, single projectile travel,
checkpoint recovery and later completion conditions. This is not a full survival-balance signoff. Live composition and
human pacing review remain pending; the game was not opened. Screenshots supplied for Prototype 44 are preserved.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 44 — archived experiment, superseded:</strong> The isolated twenty-second opening helped
expose spawn scheduling and collision issues, but its timed stop misunderstood Sean’s intent. Prototype 45 embeds the
opening into the first level instead. The <a href="design/first-call-action/report.html">original design report</a>
and prior build remain preserved; their separate-trial instructions are historical. Pickups, the playable Clogfather,
and expansion of the new encounter roles through later rooms remain planned. Only one Clogfather may appear at a time.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 40 — larger fly swarms:</strong> Swarm artwork is twice as wide and tall (128×128 display canvas), including death animation; center registration and contact core stay unchanged. Optional health bars move above the enlarged art. Includes the approved BJ completion-line revision with neutral portrait. Export/signing and packaged swarm/completion checks pass; visual review and screenshots await permission.</p>
<p><strong>Run-cycle revision — deferred after Art review:</strong> Art rejected the replacement eight-frame
candidates because leg identity, loop continuity and arm registration remain unresolved. Prototype 45 still
retains the existing six-frame animations; the foot-wiggle defect is not claimed fixed. No user decision is needed to
keep investigating. See the <a href="handoffs/hero-run-cycle-revision.json">review decision</a> and
<a href="previews/hero-run-cycle-v4.html">unapproved candidate preview</a>.</p>
<p><strong>October 16 art correction:</strong> Sean’s dispenser sheet now matches his recovered original photo with a fuller gray chin beard and distinct soul patch; the tiny-tuft revision is superseded. <a href="assets/world/spare-employee-dispenser/manifest-v4.json">Revised art manifest</a> is integrated in Prototype 41; <a href="handoffs/sean-facial-hair-audit.json">other Sean sprite sheets updated</a>: six revised sheets have the fuller gray beard and soul patch; Prototype 41 uses the revised runtime manifests and legacy sheet. Current dialogue portraits pass this check. Runtime visual review remains pending.</p>
<p><strong>Dispenser impact art revision:</strong> Tony and Sean now have versioned X-eye impact/slide poses and separate blood trails. <a href="assets/world/spare-employee-dispenser/manifest-v4.json">Art manifest v4</a> preserves the existing screen anchor and timing; Prototype 41 integrates the slide/fade; live visual review remains pending.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 41 — Spare Employee Dispenser:</strong> Integrated replacement for tape checkpoints, with Art’s machine and both hero sequences. Injured check-in scans, compresses and throws the hero into a bloody X-eyed screen splat/slide; the trail fades while an intact replacement emerges, looks around and shrugs. Full sequence targets 5.5 seconds with a 7-second watchdog, full-health stamp 0.4 seconds, checkpoint respawn 1.9 seconds. Combat freezes, progress and lives are preserved, and release/skip/menu/restart clear effects and sequence audio. Later uses are skippable with held-input protection. Sean’s corrected gameplay beard and soul patch are also integrated. Export/signing and packaged dispenser, animation, checkpoint, dialogue and input checks pass. Tony’s full-route bot completes in 134.2 seconds; Sean still exhausts lives in section four. Actual visual choreography and sound mix remain unreviewed.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 39 — sewer swarms:</strong> Two optional first-level swarms use seeded, smooth non-hunting flight, obstacle avoidance, short hovers and actual-velocity animation. Twelve HP, shared 1.5-second target cooldowns, incidental damage to plumbers and ordinary monsters, finite death, checkpoint persistence and fresh-run reset. Art supplied corrected v3 slicing of the v2 sheet. Twenty seeded one-minute corner/door simulations pass; Tony completes the automated route, while Sean still exhausts lives in section four. Export/signing and packaged mechanics checks pass. Live visual review remains pending; Sean’s full-route bot failure is unresolved. Name/lore remain proposals.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 42 — pause and mechanical feedback:</strong> B closes ordinary pause and resumes the current job, independent of button focus; A confirms the selected button. Death/Game Over remain separate. Door latch/motor/end-stop cues now follow actual gate transitions, pause/freeze and cleanup. Dispenser throws choose one random safe impact point with full-body bounds and HUD clearance, reused by the splat and slide. Export/signing and six packaged regression suites pass. Live visual/audio review remains pending.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 38 — sliding service doors:</strong> Cleared encounters lower their shutters into the floor over 0.9 seconds. Visible panels and collision stay aligned; pause freezes movement, checkpoint recovery preserves progress, and a fresh run restores closed doors. Existing encounter requirements remain unchanged. Running shots now collide using their visible thickness against enemies and walls, preserving barrel alignment, damage and range. Packaged door, running-shot, aiming, animation, death and checkpoint checks pass; screenshots await permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 37 — BJ death popup:</strong> Twelve approved messages select matching emotional portraits. Each death keeps one random message without immediate repeats; Continue preserves checkpoint progress while lives remain, and Retry starts fresh at Game Over. Held-input protection prevents accidental dismissal. Packaged popup, hero lifecycle, opening and pause-menu checks pass; screenshots await permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 36 — company name:</strong> Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply is the working employer name in employee selection, the opening introduction, Controls and entrance signage. Drain Damage remains the game title; Discharge Quarterly remains the magazine. Historical art and provenance are preserved. Game-over candidate lines remain unselected and unimplemented.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 35 — moving plumbers and three lives:</strong> Body animation is independent of aim/fire: six run frames per hero, takeoff/rise/apex/fall/landing poses, stationary hurt and nonlooping death. Grounded diagonal-down aiming is supported; only straight down requires a jump. The HUD shows one selected-hero head per remaining life. Death consumes one of three total lives, falls to a surface and respawns at the checkpoint; zero lives opens Game Over with Retry and Return to Main Menu. Runtime checks cover 240 animation combinations, life transitions and input safety. Tony completes the automated full route; the Sean bot runs out of lives, so Sean difficulty remains an open playtest issue. Art stride/shoulder polish and live visual review/screenshots remain pending.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 34 — employee checklists:</strong> Each hero’s three traits now appear on separate checked-box lines. A shared list renderer handles Tony, Sean and future profiles, with wrapped rows and spacing below the biography. Checkbox availability, paper bounds and both employee selection routes pass headless checks. Live screenshot capture awaits permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 33 — held aim and fairer turns:</strong> Art’s layered standing/airborne holds now follow continuous aim, including downward airborne directions, without requiring a shot. Projectiles use the matching mirrored muzzle; walls block barrel-through-wall shots. Pause provides selectable Resume and Return to Main Menu buttons for keyboard, controller and mouse. Flushfiends brake and stop for one second before reversing, then accelerate. Headless regressions and full-level bot runs pass for both heroes; live visual review/screenshots remain pending. Walking/recoil animation cycles and final pose refinement remain unfinished.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 32 — revised opening:</strong> Storyboarding’s seven-line introduction is integrated with explicit emotional tones and wrapped text. Both employee routes, fresh-run triggering, skip/input guards and unchanged completion scenes pass headless checks. Live screenshots await permission. Persistent visible aiming remains unfinished.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 31 — employee snapshots:</strong> Selection portraits share Art’s taped instant-photo frame, muted backdrop, live first-name caption and common tilt. Reusable for future hero entries; dialogue portraits unchanged. Layout bounds and selection regressions checked headlessly; live review/screenshots pending permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 30 — illustrated punch clock:</strong> Art’s worn teal mechanical clock and paper timecard replace the code-drawn panel. The CLOCK IN label and click target align with the brass button; keyboard/controller confirmation and Tony default selection are retained. Headless checks and export verified; live screenshots pending permission.</p>
<p><strong>Prototype 29 — current branding cleanup:</strong> HUD and current build/help text use Drain Damage. Service signage and employee paperwork use neutral wording while the employer name is undecided. Export is now builds/Drain Damage.app. Historical archives, screenshots and stable bundle identity remain intact. Art audited the current title, controls, portraits, sprites, clipboard and scenery and found no old branding baked into those images. Headless checks and export are verified; fresh screenshots await permission.</p>
<p><strong>October 15 MacBook playtest refresh:</strong> All six agents consulted; no additional approved runtime assets or mechanics were waiting. Prototype 28 was rebuilt and its packaged aiming, entrances, controller controls, music, dialogue and full-route completion checked. Modular character art remains a provisional mockup. Screenshots and live playtest await launch permission. <a href="handoffs/playtest-build-2026-10-15.json">Build verification record</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Expanded first-level route — integrated in Prototype 27:</strong> Six zones span 9,600 logical pixels with 30 finite Flushfiends, a four-enemy/warning cap, three tape checkpoints, 17 grounded machinery props and visible encounter shutters. Both player and enemy movement respect solid sides/tops; projectiles use the same geometry. Reinforcements use 1.25-second harmless warnings and safe visible placement, with forward spawns preferred. The final encounter is a finite 3+2 toilet-wave fallback. Clogfather, hazards, portal and new zone background variants remain deferred; the intended boss mission is not claimed complete. Scripted full-route runs finish with Tony in 93.75s and Sean in 139.73s, including bot respawns; these are not human pacing measurements and do not validate the 4–6 minute target. Approved small-preview screenshots now cover selection and the service entry. Tony defaults to 1/2, Clock In is clear, and pipe-bundle surfaces and pursuing enemies were visually checked. Later machinery, shutters and finale remain pending live review; preview closed.</p>
<p><strong>Friend playtest package:</strong> Prototype 26 is available as <a href="builds/share/Drain-Damage-0.26.0-macOS.zip">a shareable macOS ZIP</a> with the standalone app and setup guide. Universal arm64/x86_64 binary; declared minimum macOS 13 on Apple Silicon and 11 on Intel. Intel hardware and first launch on another Mac remain untested. Ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized; Apple’s per-app approval steps are included. This packages the same build, with no gameplay changes.</p>
<p><strong>Engineering validation:</strong> Headless checks cover both-character traversal, actual persistent enemy pursuit across props in both directions, gate camping, finite counts, warning cancellation, checkpoint/reset, descent shooting, menus and approved dialogue. Full-route scripted runs use real movement and weapons rather than forced kills. Existing shutdown object-leak warnings remain. Final layout and metrics are in <a href="handoffs/first-call-integration.json">the integration handoff</a>. The earlier Prototype 26 friend ZIP remains an explicitly older build.</p>
<p>Prototype 26 integrates persistent toilet pursuit after detection, without a home leash or distance timeout. Patrol bounds apply only before aggro; surviving enemies retain pursuit across checkpoint respawn. Canonical weapon tuning is live: Tony damage 6, range 320; Sean damage 24, range 480. Firing intervals remain 0.15s and 1.0s. A 40-HP toilet takes seven Tony hits or two Sean hits. Headless checks cover pursuit, hit counts, swept collision and range caps. Boss timing remains pending retuning; no new boss encounter is implemented.</p>
<p>Prototype 25 replaces basement completion dialogue with the two approved seven-line routes. The other plumber is labeled radio support; BJ dispatches another address as narrative setup only. Existing victory, skip, retry and title behavior is retained. No new level is implied. Headless validation and export are checked; screenshots remain pending permission.</p>
<p>October 15: replacement <a href="assets/selection/punch-clock-v1.png">industrial punch-clock artwork</a> delivered, with an analog dial, timecard slot and brass button matching the clipboard. <a href="assets/selection/punch-clock.json">Crop, live-label placement and click-target handoff</a> saved. Integrated in Prototype 30 and included in Prototype 31; menu-size visual review remains pending permission.</p>
<p>Prototype 24 moves Clock In to a separate code-drawn punch-clock panel beside the clipboard, with a clear button and matching click target. Tony (1/2) is selected on launch and every time employee selection opens. Packaged selection regression checks cover the default and non-overlapping button bounds. Live visual review and fresh screenshots await permission.</p>
<p><strong>Art workflow:</strong> Whenever new artwork is needed, Engineering asks Bestiary / Art for help, supplies layout and runtime requirements, and integrates the delivered assets.</p>
<p><strong>Art direction:</strong> Salvage Special replaces the rejected cheese direction. Original concepts and approvals remain preserved. Delivered: the Storyboarding employee-file selection redesign and initial relative movement/health tuning; visual review and balance playtesting remain pending. Tony’s approved biography is recorded in <a href="assets/selection/approved-copy.json">selection copy</a>: “A fourth-generation plumber with decades of experience installing, building, and keeping essential systems running.” This supersedes the earlier fixing-pipes biography; other requested selection details remain unchanged.</p>
<p>Prototype 19 adds the approved seven-line Billy-Joe introduction after character selection, once per fresh run. Shared scene and emotional portraits for either hero; visible binding-aware Skip, typewriter advance, frozen action, and held-input protection. Death, checkpoint respawn, and retry do not replay it. This is story dialogue, not a tutorial. Brief skippable discovery scenes between levels are approved direction; future scripts/locations remain undecided. In-game visual review and new screenshots await permission.</p>
<p>Prototype 18 integrates the current Drain Damage title/menu artwork and all 30 Tony, Sean, and BJ emotional portraits. The runtime renderer and muzzle now use the same pose independently of firing. Provisional static holds replace the older walk/fire frames; locomotion/recoil animation and live visual approval remain open.</p>
<p><strong>Septic Air Force — sewer-fly swarm:</strong> October 16: Sean selected <em>Septic Air Force</em> as the working swarm name. Revised aviation-themed lore is drafted; Gnatastrophe is saved as a possible future boss name only; <a href="handoffs/sewer-fly-story.json">editorial handoff</a> ready. Prototype 39 integrates initial 12 HP tuning with corrected v3 slicing; live animation readability and balance remain pending. <a href="bestiary/sewer-flies/preview.html">Preview</a>.</p>

Test simultaneous touches and Bluetooth controller input on each OS.</p></li><li><h3>Phone-sized usability</h3><p>Check notches/safe areas, aspect ratios, readable text, pause/resume, audio interruptions, heat, battery use, and frame pacing.</p></li><li><h3>Write the feasibility verdict</h3><p>For each platform: install steps, signing/renewal friction, test results, blockers, estimated effort, and go/defer recommendation.</p></li></ul><p class="gate">Done means: a real-device prototype runs on each target, or a concrete blocker is documented. Mobile release is not yet committed.</p></section>

<section class="notes" aria-labelledby="mobile-notes">
<h2 id="mobile-notes">Mobile install options: what we know so far</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Already cross-platform:</strong> our Godot/GDScript project can target macOS, Android, and iOS.
<a href="https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/export/index.html">Godot export documentation</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Reuse the game:</strong> gameplay, levels, artwork, and most code should carry over; a language rewrite
is not required to investigate mobile versions.</li>
<li><strong>Mobile work:</strong> add touch controls, adapt layouts and safe areas, and test controller input,
performance, audio, and app suspension on real devices.</li>
<li><strong>Separate packages:</strong> produce an Android APK and an iOS development build with the necessary
platform tools and signing. Neither mobile version has been validated yet.</li>
<li><strong>Kotlin comparison:</strong> Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose can share code and UI across these platforms;
our current recommendation is to keep Godot for this action game. No migration is planned.
<a href="https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/faq.html">Kotlin Multiplatform FAQ</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Android:</strong> investigate a signed APK installed directly on a test device, using developer deployment
or the device’s permitted local-install flow. Confirm the actual OS, device and regional requirements when testing.
Godot provides an Android export path requiring Java and Android SDK setup.
<a href="https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/export/exporting_for_android.html">Godot Android export guide</a>.</p>
<p><strong>iOS:</strong> the initial equivalent is a development build installed from Xcode on the Mac.
Godot exports an Xcode project; public App Store publication is not required for this test.
<a href="https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/export/exporting_for_ios.html">Godot iOS export guide</a>.</p>
<p>A free Apple Account can use an Xcode Personal Team for personal-device testing, with limitations including
seven-day provisioning profiles that require rebuilding/reinstalling after expiry. Evaluate paid-program development,
ad hoc distribution or TestFlight only if we need broader testing.
<a href="https://developer.apple.com/help/account/basics/about-your-developer-account">Apple account and testing limits</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Research gate:</strong> verify these paths with our installed Godot/Xcode versions and actual devices.
A successful export alone does not prove that touch controls, performance, or signing are practical.</p>
</section>
<section class="notes" aria-labelledby="working-rules">
<h2 id="working-rules">How we keep this manageable</h2>
<ul>
<li>Ask Sean and wait for permission before opening or foregrounding the game for a playtest or inspection.
Keep agent checks headless/background; ask first if a visual test would interrupt him. Approved playtests use a large window.</li>
<li>Keep Mac playable throughout. Mobile research can start early; full ports follow evidence.</li>
<li>Preserve the satisfying jump and forgiving retries. Let playtesting drive changes.</li>
<li>Archive screenshots and notes for every delivered game build. Keep earlier chapters intact.</li>
<li>Use original or licensed assets and document their sources.</li>
<li>Agree on the next small milestone before expanding the game. No calendar deadlines are committed here.</li>
</ul>
</section>
<footer>This is the project’s editable roadmap, not a completion percentage or a promise of every idea.
Filters only change this view; milestone status is maintained in this HTML file. No external scripts, fonts, or tracking.</footer>
</main>
<script>
const filters = document.querySelectorAll('[data-filter]');
const phases = document.querySelectorAll('.phase');
filters.forEach(button => button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const selected = button.dataset.filter;
  let visible = 0;
  filters.forEach(filter => filter.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(filter === button)));
  phases.forEach(phase => {
    phase.hidden = selected !== 'all' && phase.dataset.status !== selected;
    if (!phase.hidden) visible += 1;
  });
  document.getElementById('filter-status').textContent =
    `Showing ${visible} ${visible === 1 ? 'milestone' : 'milestones'}${selected === 'all' ? ' across all tracks' : ''}.`;
}));
</script>

SHA-256: `65959a633b7edbedf53634e8f10e9748209f7962b0499ce5b9a80777b1296beb`

````text
# Discharge Quarterly

[magazine.json](magazine.json) is the canonical editable source for the magazine. It contains publication metadata,
ordered pages, text, captions, image references and layout templates. The PDF is generated output.

## Editing and building

1. Edit the relevant page by its stable `id`. Edit `text` for headings and paragraphs; retain paragraph markup such
   as `<b>` and `<br/>`. Asset paths are relative to the project root.
2. Adjust element coordinates and sizes when needed. Coordinates use PDF points from the bottom left; paragraph
   `top` is the top edge. Images and selected crops fit their box without distortion.
3. For a new edition, update publication metadata, visible edition/date text, page templates and the output path.
   Keep earlier PDFs intact. Keep page numbers sequential and update the contents when inserting pages.
4. Run from the project root with Python and ReportLab installed:

   ```shell
   python3 marketing/magazine/build_guide.py
   ```

5. Render the PDF with `pdftoppm` and inspect every page before delivery. The renderer rejects paragraph overflow,
   missing images and unknown element types, but visual review remains necessary.

The renderer uses the macOS fonts configured in `layout.font_directory`. Change that path and the font filenames
if building elsewhere. Shared header/footer templates use `{page_number}` and `{section}` placeholders.

## Edition 20 portraits

Edition 20 uses Art's new hyperreal Tony and Sean portraits on page 2. The rendered crew page was visually checked;
all eight pages retain the previous edition's text apart from the edition number. Earlier PDFs are preserved.
Portrait provenance is recorded in `handoffs/hero-hyperreal-marketing-portraits.json` at the project root.

## Edition 19 feedback integration

Edition 19 incorporates the October 16 review: Storyboarding's subtle dispenser feature copy, glass-front
Tony/Sean-stocked machine artwork, Tony's Clogfather reaction, the requested Widow wording, and removal of tentative
preview and development-history captions. The approved fake-advertisement headline and tone are retained.
All eight pages were rendered and visually inspected; extracted text was reviewed. Earlier editions are preserved.
The source before integration is archived in `guide-assets-v19/pre-publication-source.json`.

## Edition 21 disclaimer removal

Removed the fictional-company footer and fictional-publication/non-affiliation paragraph. All eight pages rendered
and visually checked; extracted text audited. `current.pdf` matches edition 21.

## Editorial policy

Do not include fictional-company, fictional-publication or non-affiliation disclaimers in the reader edition.

Suggest the dispenser's disturbing corporate practices through euphemisms and omissions. Do not describe its
lethal mechanism or bodily processing. Never mention the viewer's screen or other fourth-wall-breaking details.

Write for people who love games. Assume no knowledge of game design or development. This rule applies to the
cover, contents, profiles, headings, captions, sidebars, credits and PDF metadata, not just body paragraphs.
Describe what readers can see or experience. Player terms such as health, attacks, checkpoint and reload are fine.

Keep sprite-sheet terminology, atlas details, frame counts, build IDs, runtime/integration status, collision rules,
validation notes and agent/process commentary out of the publication. Do not disguise technical explanations with
new headings: remove row/column/frame-count descriptions. Keep technical records in internal manifests and this
README. The `editorial_guidance` object in the JSON is internal guidance and is not rendered.

Remove tentative captions such as “Preview artwork,” “An idea we're exploring,” and “This account is still
taking shape.” Keep production status and image provenance in internal records. Picture captions should describe
the subject, action, atmosphere or useful player information. Do not discuss earlier versions, development history,
prototype status or production progress in the magazine. Never imply unfinished encounters are playable.

Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must use `TODO: <specific missing item>` in a conspicuous high-contrast
box with bold type at least 18 pt. Allow enough space to prevent clipping. Never hide TODOs in small italic captions
or vague caveats. Existing artwork does not need a TODO merely because gameplay remains unfinished.

Keep future plot spoilers, creature-origin explanations and boss solutions out of promotional copy. Preserve
approved profiles and lore, current names, and honest qualifications for unsettled stories. Preserve historical
screenshots and earlier editions. Request new illustrations through Bestiary / Art. Do not change mechanics or
canonical creature records while editing the magazine.

Extract the complete PDF text and audit it for development jargon, including bookmarks and metadata. Render and
visually inspect every affected page after rewriting; check that shorter copy still fits the layout naturally.

Follow the writing-style guidance in `../../AGENTS.md`. Prefer natural, varied sentences and specific observations
rather than repeated paired fragments or generic dramatic contrasts. Review headings, captions and body copy for
repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.

## Edition 18 editorial revision

Edition 18 retains the eight-page design and revises repetitive headlines, captions and promotional copy.
Approved character and creature lore remains intact. The complete extracted text was reviewed and all eight
rendered pages were visually checked. Edition 17's source is archived in `guide-assets-v18/`.

## Edition 17 layout direction

Use the supplied 1990s Nintendo Power and GamePro spreads as the visual reference: large shadowed display type,
bright section banners, compact columns, small bordered pictures, cutout characters and conversational captions.
Vary the page composition by feature. Avoid returning to one large portrait and several pages per creature.

The eight-page issue contains a cover, paired crew profiles, BJ and dispenser half-page features, a two-page
creature roundup, a gameplay feature, one curated action gallery and an in-universe back-cover advertisement.
Keep full animation sheets out of the reader edition. Select a few complete poses for the action gallery and
inspect the crops against their actual artwork boundaries. Preserve proportions and original files.

All layout elements and text remain in `magazine.json`. Display text supports `angle`, `outline` and
`stroke_width`; paragraphs support an optional `font`. Font choices remain in the JSON layout settings.

## Automatic web publication

The PDF generator also refreshes `current.pdf`, the stable Git LFS publication file. After visual review, commit
and push that file to `main`. The **Publish magazine** GitHub Actions workflow renders its pages and deploys
only the reader, page images, and downloadable PDF to GitHub Pages. Local generation alone does not publish.

The HTML reader reproduces the PDF pages as images rather than reflowing the design. It includes page navigation
and the original PDF for selectable text and full-resolution zoom. Image-only pages are not a screen-reader
replacement for the document. GitHub Actions uses the finished PDF, so macOS fonts are not needed on the server.

Expected address: [Discharge Quarterly](https://jugglingbear.github.io/drain-damage/).
The workflow can also be rerun manually from GitHub Actions. Failed builds leave the previous deployment intact.

To preview the generated site locally with Poppler installed:

```sh
python3 tools/build_magazine_site.py
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory builds/magazine-site
```

Open `http://localhost:8000` in a browser. Generated site files stay in the ignored builds folder.
````

        },
        {
          "id": "crew-033",

            1122

        {
          "id": "crew-034",

          "y": 354,
          "w": 270,
          "h": 24,
          "color": "E62A32"
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-035",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "SEAN",
          "x": 326,
          "y": 351,
          "size": 25,
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-036",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "THE APPRENTICE",
          "x": 318,
          "y": 330,
          "size": 15,
          "color": "E62A32",
          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-037",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Sean wandered in looking for work and somehow ended up on Tony's crew. He's willing to help, although it's worth checking what he's holding before asking him to hand you a tool. Tony is showing him the ropes. There are quite a few ropes.",
          "x": 318,
          "top": 323,
          "width": 270,
          "size": 11.5,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 100,
          "leading": 12.88
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-038",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "FIRST DAY",
          "x": 318,
          "y": 210,
          "size": 14,
          "color": "E62A32",
          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-039",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Sean arrived without much knowledge of plumbing. Tony took him on anyway. For now, enthusiasm is doing a lot of the work, and a patient teacher is keeping the rest moving.",
          "x": 318,
          "top": 203,
          "width": 270,
          "size": 11,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 85,
          "leading": 12.32
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-040",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 318,
          "y": 47,
          "w": 270,
          "h": 64,
          "color": "FFF000"
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-041",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "TOOL TALK",
          "x": 327,
          "y": 93,
          "size": 13,
          "color": "111421",
          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "crew-042",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Sean's heavy plunger launcher hits hard. Make each shot count, and leave yourself room while he reloads.",
          "x": 327,
          "top": 86,
          "width": 252,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 35,
          "leading": 11.760000000000002
        }
      ]
    },

          "id": "management-maintenance-013",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "CALL HIM BJ.",

          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "management-maintenance-014",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it might be unpleasant.",
          "x": 198,
          "top": 632,
          "width": 184,
          "size": 11.4,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 159,
          "leading": 12.768000000000002
        },
        {
          "id": "management-maintenance-015",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "BJ speaks calmly, keeps the jobs coming, and expects his employees to get on with them. If you're hoping the smiling face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.",
          "x": 400,
          "top": 632,

        },
        {
          "id": "management-maintenance-027",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply would like you to know that arrangements have been made. The Spare Employee Dispenser stands ready between service calls, its glass front offering a reassuring view of the company\u2019s preparations. There is rust around the hinges and something familiar about the occupants. The accompanying leaflet describes them as reserve personnel. It asks employees to respect their rest and directs all further questions to the same leaflet.",
          "x": 24,
          "top": 273,
          "width": 196,
          "size": 11,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 170,
          "leading": 12.32
        },
        {
          "id": "management-maintenance-028",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "The leaflet is particularly clear on continuity of service. Your assignments will remain on the schedule, your tools will still be required, and your name will stay on the rota. Several paragraphs explain how much the company values an experienced employee. The section headed \u201cWhat this means for you\u201d refers back to those paragraphs. We would have preferred a little more detail, but the cabinet does appear to be well stocked.",

          "top": 273,
          "width": 185,

        {
          "id": "creature-feature-one-015",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "This bad-tempered fixture has burning red eyes under a lid-like brow, ceramic teeth around its bowl, and short pipe legs. It patrols until a plumber gets too close, then closes the distance with a hop. The service appointment is unlikely to go as planned.",
          "x": 244,
          "top": 609,
          "width": 342,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 104,
          "leading": 13.440000000000001
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-one-016",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "<b>Service tip:</b> Look for pipe legs, red eyes and teeth around the bowl. If it starts following you, the appointment has moved beyond routine maintenance.",

          "size": 26,

          "outline": "FFFFFF",

        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-one-024",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.",
          "x": 244,
          "top": 318,
          "width": 342,
          "size": 11.5,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 161,
          "leading": 12.88

          "path": "bestiary/clogfather/marketing-v1.png",
          "x": 340,
          "y": 411,
          "width": 246,
          "height": 246,
          "crop": null
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-012",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "03 / A BLOCKAGE WITH AMBITION",
          "x": 26,
          "y": 642,
          "size": 14,
          "color": "008C70",
          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-013",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences back at anyone approaching.",
          "x": 26,
          "top": 629,
          "width": 291,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 111,
          "leading": 13.440000000000001
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-016",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 24,
          "y": 59,
          "w": 564,
          "h": 300,
          "color": "CFECEC"
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-017",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "SEPTIC AIR FORCE",
          "x": 37,
          "y": 310,
          "size": 35,
          "color": "111421",
          "font": "Display",
          "angle": 0
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-018",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "SEPTIC AIR FORCE",
          "x": 35,
          "y": 312,
          "size": 35,
          "color": "1744B9",
          "font": "Display",
          "angle": 0,
          "outline": "FFFFFF",
          "stroke_width": 0.35
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-019",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "04 / STILL WAITING FOR LANDING CLEARANCE",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 285,
          "size": 14,
          "color": "E62A32",
          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-020",
          "type": "image",
          "path": "assets/bestiary/sewer-flies/swarm-mockup-v2.png",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 113,
          "width": 154,
          "height": 154,
          "crop": [
            0,
            0,
            256,
            256
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-021",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.",
          "x": 206,
          "top": 267,
          "width": 369,
          "size": 11.5,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 157,
          "leading": 12.88
        },
        {
          "id": "creature-feature-two-022",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "This tight cloud of flies hurts plumbers and monsters alike when they cross its path.",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 111,
          "width": 154,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "111421",
          "max_height": 42,
          "leading": 11.760000000000002
        },
        {
          "id": "clogfather-tony-reaction",

          "width": 172,
          "height": 172,
          "crop": null
        }
      ]
    },

        },
        {

        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-009",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "LEAVE YOURSELF ROOM BEFORE THE FLUSHFIEND STARTS HOPPING.",
          "x": 26,
          "y": 686,
          "size": 14,
          "color": "00BADA",

        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-010",

          "h": 208,
          "color": "FFF000"
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-011",
          "type": "image",
          "path": "marketing/magazine/guide-assets-v1/toilet-action-1.png",
          "x": 26,
          "y": 461,
          "width": 362,
          "height": 204,
          "crop": [
            0,
            63,

            541
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-012",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 408,
          "y": 641,
          "w": 178,
          "h": 24,
          "color": "1744B9"
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-013",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "ON YOUR TOES",
          "x": 416,
          "y": 645,
          "size": 18,
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "font": "Condensed"
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-014",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "A moving fixture is your cue to back away. By the time it reaches your boots, you will want more room than you left yourself.",
          "x": 408,
          "top": 626,
          "width": 178,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "max_height": 125,
          "leading": 13.440000000000001
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-015",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "<b>FIELD TIP:</b> Keep some clear floor behind you. A wall is a poor escape route.",
          "x": 408,
          "top": 506,
          "width": 178,
          "size": 11,
          "color": "FFF000",
          "max_height": 71,
          "leading": 12.32
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-017",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "DON'T LET IT CLOSE THE GAP.",
          "x": 27,
          "y": 384,
          "size": 29,
          "color": "111421",
          "font": "Display",
          "angle": 0
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-018",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "DON'T LET IT CLOSE THE GAP.",
          "x": 25,
          "y": 386,
          "size": 29,
          "color": "00BADA",
          "font": "Display",
          "angle": 0,
          "outline": "FFFFFF",
          "stroke_width": 0.35
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-019",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "The toilet follows Sean and hurts him when it catches him. After a hit, you have a brief chance to get clear before it can hurt you again. Use it.",
          "x": 26,
          "top": 367,
          "width": 174,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "max_height": 120,
          "leading": 13.440000000000001
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-020",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Tony can keep the pressure on with quick shots. Sean needs a little more breathing room between heavy plungers. Either way, standing still gives the teeth time to catch up.",
          "x": 218,
          "top": 367,
          "width": 174,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "max_height": 120,
          "leading": 13.440000000000001
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-021",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Watch the floor ahead as well as the creature behind. You need room for the next shot, the next landing and whatever the building has decided to do next.",
          "x": 410,
          "top": 367,
          "width": 176,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "max_height": 120,
          "leading": 13.440000000000001
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-022",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 24,
          "y": 78,
          "w": 268,
          "h": 153,
          "color": "00BADA"
        },

        {
          "id": "on-the-job-026",

          "text": "<b>Leave room for the hop</b> before lining up another shot.",
          "x": 26,
          "top": 69,
          "width": 264,
          "size": 11,
          "color": "FFF000",
          "max_height": 25,
          "leading": 12.32
        },
        {
          "id": "on-the-job-027",

          "top": 69,
          "width": 264,
