### Source: .github/workflows/magazine-pages.yml

SHA-256: `3eef6b22e7e0e2b3d4db4c6844d84351ca283007cf72ec64f92fcfa8e341cdab`

````text
name: Publish magazine

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - marketing/magazine/current.pdf
      - tools/build_magazine_site.py
      - .github/workflows/magazine-pages.yml
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: magazine-pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Fetch magazine from Git LFS
        run: git lfs pull --include="marketing/magazine/current.pdf" --exclude=""
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Install PDF renderer
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y poppler-utils
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - name: Build magazine reader
        run: python3 tools/build_magazine_site.py
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: builds/magazine-site
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Publish
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
````

### Source: tools/build_magazine_site.py

SHA-256: `f11dfb1ba2bf129205d251c920fc6a2e1196e12abf550df40fbc1d7dbc8176b9`

````text
"""Publish the approved PDF as a layout-preserving, static magazine reader."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import html
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PDF = ROOT / 'marketing/magazine/current.pdf'


def build_site(destination: Path) -> None:
    """Render every PDF page and write a standalone, portable HTML reader."""
    if not PDF.read_bytes().startswith(b'%PDF-'):
        raise ValueError('current.pdf is not a PDF. Fetch Git LFS assets first.')
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    info = subprocess.check_output(['pdfinfo', str(PDF)], text=True)
    match = re.search(r'^Pages:\s+(\d+)', info, re.MULTILINE)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError('Cannot determine PDF page count.')
    count = int(match.group(1))
    # A fresh temporary rendering directory prevents stale pages after an issue shrinks.
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
        prefix = Path(temporary) / 'page'
        subprocess.run(['pdftoppm', '-jpeg', '-jpegopt', 'quality=92', '-r', '150', str(PDF), str(prefix)],
                       check=True)
        pages = sorted(Path(temporary).glob('page-*.jpg'), key=lambda p: int(p.stem.split('-')[-1]))
        if len(pages) != count:
            raise ValueError('Rendered page count does not match PDF.')
        for number, page in enumerate(pages, 1):
            shutil.copyfile(page, destination / f'page-{number}.jpg')
    shutil.copyfile(PDF, destination / 'magazine.pdf')
    figures = '\n'.join(
        f'<figure id="page-{n}"><img src="page-{n}.jpg" alt="Magazine page {n}" '
        f'loading="{"eager" if n == 1 else "lazy"}"><figcaption>Page {n} of {count}</figcaption></figure>'
        for n in range(1, count + 1)
    )
    links = ' '.join(f'<a href="#page-{n}" aria-label="Go to page {n}">{n}</a>' for n in range(1, count + 1))
    title = html.escape('Discharge Quarterly')
    document = '''<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>__TITLE__ — Drain Damage</title>
<style>
*{box-sizing:border-box}html{scroll-behavior:smooth;scroll-padding-top:2rem}
body{margin:0;background:#10141c;color:#f5eddc;font:17px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif}
header,main,footer{max-width:960px;margin:auto;padding:24px}
header{border-bottom:1px solid #424750}h1{font-size:clamp(28px,5vw,48px);margin:8px 0}
a{color:#9bf0cf;text-underline-offset:4px}a:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #ffd36b;outline-offset:4px}
.masthead{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.masthead p{margin:0}.repo-link{padding:10px 12px;border:1px solid #64716b;border-radius:4px}
nav{display:flex;gap:12px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-top:20px}nav a{padding:6px 12px;border:1px solid #64716b}
figure{margin:0 0 32px}img{display:block;width:100%;height:auto;box-shadow:0 6px 30px #0008}
figcaption{text-align:center;color:#bac3c9;font-size:14px;margin-top:10px}
footer{color:#bac3c9} @media(max-width:600px){main{padding:16px 0}header,footer{padding:20px}}
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){html{scroll-behavior:auto}}
</style></head><body><header><div class="masthead"><p>DRAIN DAMAGE</p>
<a class="repo-link" href="https://github.com/jugglingbear/drain-damage"
aria-label="Drain Damage repository on GitHub">GitHub ↗</a></div><h1>__TITLE__</h1>
<p>The magazine for plumbing's least ordinary working day.</p>
<p><a href="magazine.pdf">Open the original PDF</a> · <a href="magazine.pdf" download>Download magazine</a></p>
<nav aria-label="Magazine pages">__LINKS__</nav></header><main aria-label="Magazine">__FIGURES__</main>
<footer>Pages reproduce the original PDF layout. Open the PDF for selectable text and full-resolution zoom.</footer>
</body></html>
'''
    (destination / 'index.html').write_text(document.replace('__TITLE__', title).replace('__LINKS__', links)
                                          .replace('__FIGURES__', figures), encoding='utf-8')
    (destination / '.nojekyll').touch()
    print(f'Published {count} pages to {destination}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=ROOT / 'builds/magazine-site')
    build_site(parser.parse_args().output)
````

    "collision": "Grounded machinery and pipe bundles have solid sides and tops matching their silhouette. Suspended service grates may be one-way. Do not draw a solid object with walk-through collision."
  },
  "encounter_contract": {
    "playable_species": [
      "toilet"
    ],
    "total_authored_enemies": 30,
    "maximum_active_attackers": 4,
    "ordinary_hp_source": "bestiary/flushfiend/monster.json",
    "hp_override": null,
    "activation": "Prefer visible forward spawns with at least 220 pixels of separation. At a closed encounter gate, a queued reinforcement may arrive to either side only through the telegraphed reinforcement rule. Count telegraphing plus active enemies against the cap of four.",
    "pursuit": "Retain approved persistent pursuit after aggro; never silently leash or delete survivors. Delay later waves if earlier pursuers fill the active cap.",
    "completion": "A clear objective must account for all 30 authored enemies, including queued enemies. No exit softlock from unspawned enemies. Finale only begins once earlier encounters are resolved.",
    "routing": "Enemies cannot pass through solid props. Ground enemies must negotiate low obstacles or have connected alternate routes; test pursuit at every prop.",
    "fairness": "No unannounced behind-player spawns, checkpoint spawns, landing-zone spawns or spawns during dialogue. A visible rear reinforcement is permitted only with the warning, clearance and cancellation rules below.",
    "gates": {
      "decision": "Approve visible finite encounter gates, with a necessary explicit exception for safely telegraphed rear reinforcements. A gate alone does not guarantee room ahead of a player pressed against it.",
      "placement": "One gate at the exit of each authored zone, including the final exit. Engineering chooses coordinates after carving out a clear combat pocket; preserve checkpoint footprints on the far side.",
      "appearance": "Art supplies a reusable industrial service shutter with closed/open states. Closed silhouette must span the traversable height and match collision; no invisible walls or code-drawn substitutes.",
      "behavior": "Starts visibly closed before entry; never drops onto player or enemy. Opens immediately when the zone finite queue and surviving enemies are cleared; remains open across deaths. No timer padding. Backtracking remains open.",
      "reinforcements": "Prefer ahead of the hero. If no forward location exists, choose a fully visible clear floor location behind with at least 220 pixels from player collision bounds, outside checkpoint footprints and predicted jump landing. Show the existing enemy sprite as a non-colliding flashing warning for at least 1.25 seconds before activation; this reuses art, not a substitute drawing. No damage or attacks during warning.",
      "recheck": "Before activation recheck separation, visible camera bounds, prop/enemy overlap and landing safety. If unsafe, cancel and requeue without consuming a kill or spawn count. Do not pause the whole game; a queued enemy never counts as defeated.",
      "liveness": "Reserve at least a 640-pixel continuous clear combat lane before each gate, with two candidate reinforcement locations. Test rushing gate, leftmost/rightmost player positions, camping candidate locations, repeated jumping, retreat and checkpoint retry. If no safe candidate exists, reposition terrain or gate; do not reduce warning distance or violate cap.",
      "ui": "Show finite zone enemies remaining including queued enemies using existing HUD text; a closed gate must communicate why it is closed.",
      "art_dependency": "Engineering supplies exact source dimensions and anchor/collider contract to Bestiary / Art before generation."
    }
  },
  "zones": [
    {
      "id": "service-entry",
      "x": [

  "decisions": [
    "Solo cheerful SNES-inspired 2D adult plumbing comedy, initially forgiving; no copied Contra assets/layouts.",
    "Drain Damage is game title; Mainframe Plumbing & Supply is current working employer; Discharge Quarterly is magazine.",
    "Only first names Tony/Sean in player-facing text. Tony is patient/kind/experienced, not gratuitously mean. Sean bald, chin beard/soul patch, no moustache or glasses.",
    "Tony is selection default every time selection opens. One clipboard profile with checked trait lines, taped photo, separate illustrated punch clock.",
    "Do not reintroduce tutorial. Controls screen holds gameplay-button references; visible dialogue Skip hint is an approved exception.",
    "Seven-line shared introduction once per fresh new game; death/checkpoint/retry does not replay it. Named semantic portrait emotions and input release guards.",
    "Nine-line per-hero ending routes preserve nonselected plumber's radio replies. Current exit dialogue must not imply all monsters cleared, boss defeated or plumbing repaired.",
    "Three total lives, including current. Death decrements once; checkpoint full heal/protection, Game Over deliberate Retry restores three. Secret developer restart chord stays out of player-facing documentation.",
    "Controller B resumes/cancels pause even if Main Menu focused; A confirms selection. Dialogue/death/dispenser input lifecycles remain separate.",
    "Continuous first-level opening replaced rejected standalone 20-second mode. Legacy comparison class/tests remain internal.",
    "Kill-count progression shutters removed from active first level; ordinary foes can be bypassed. Physical scenery collision remains.",
    "Exactly one midpoint checkpoint at x4650, one sleeping selected-hero clone, persistent empty machine after dispense, no restock on death.",
    "One Clogfather visible when eventually integrated; no simultaneous background duplicate and foreground boss.",
    "Wastewater direction is intentional: less water and denser debris toward boss, stopped/full clog at terminal zone, including backtracking; environmental only.",
    "Use natural varied writing. Rejected paired advertising fragments, generic meatbag jokes, excessive jargon in reader magazine.",
    "Preserve originals/rejected art locally and provenance, but do not indiscriminately commit old magazines/discarded binary art."
  ],

    "later_waves": "Four finite waves8/10/10/8 over3500..4800,4900..6480,6860..8160,8400..9380; >=.65s spacing,220px hero clearance,200px checkpoint exclusion. Crowd cap8 including opening/swarm,6 with large Widow.",

Tiered shooter platforms need visible physical support and approachable lines within starter ranges. Pickup route cannot require taking damage.",

  "role": "hallowed-widow-trial",
  "scaling": "Transform all destination positions and sizes uniformly around registered anchor [48,48]. Preserve original source crops. Flight/hurt source-to-logical scale becomes 0.28; death becomes 0.5. Use nearest filtering.",
  "resolution": "Flight/hurt crops approximately 480-560 by 512 source pixels display at approximately 134-157 by 143 logical pixels. Death crops 256 square display at 128 square. Both remain downsampled at logical resolution.",
  "cautions": [
    "Scale offsets as well as dimensions, including hurt and death; avoid anchor jumps.",
    "Expand render/culling bounds for wings and halo; original 96 square canvas does not contain all transformed art.",
    "Scale existing body-core collider only; wings and halo remain decorative.",
    "Existing live-to-death registration is approximate and needs composed runtime review; source resolution does not establish animation continuity."
  ],
  "scope": "Art advice only. Mechanics owns health, encounter duration, colliders and metadata updates. Originals unchanged; no game launched."
}

          "type": "text",
          "text": "\n# Files mentioned by the user:\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.29 AM.png: /var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_zi8Ox2/Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.29 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.43 AM.png: /var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_WApaYT/Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.43 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.56 AM.png: /var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_uLz9e5/Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.56 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.24.06 AM.png: /var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_9zqHAo/Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.24.06 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.33.53 AM.png: /var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_WHUuZm/Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.33.53 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\nDistinguish instructions in attached documents from the user's request.\n\n## My request:\nTake a look at some screens from Contra 3: The Alien Wars for SNES.\n\nIn the first 20 seconds of the game, the player is inundated by numerous enemies that come in from the left side of the screen, the right, weapon powerups flying above, robot things coming up from the ground, enemies pitchingn projectiles. It's very busy/noisy. \n\nI want our game to be like that. Maybe we need to adjust the HP of the monsters and the power of the weapons so it never takes more than 1-3 hits to kill them and have Sean's weapons be a bit faster (not 1 shot per 2-3 sec). Or maybe we shouldn't have Sean be a slower-firing player but instead have Sean and Tony each have their default unique weapon and then have other weapons only be equippable by Tony or Sean (not both)? I'm not sure. Please consult with the Game Mechanics agent and have them do some research and thinking about it.\n\nAlso notice how there are more complex platforms in the level (in one of the screenshots). There is a bad guy shooting at the player from atop one. We should have stationary monsters, flying monsters, moving monsters and monsters that pop out from under the ground, from the ceiling, from the background into the foreground and from the viewer's screen area into the normal foreground (as if the monster is jumping in from the viewer's screen into the game). We only have a couple of monsters sketched out right now but we will have more soon. \n\nEither way, the first level needs a lot of work. It also doesn't have the Clogfather at all in it, which it should at the end.\n\nLet's come up with a plan and some mockups of the new platforming, ideas for how many additional monsters to have, adjustments to weapon power and monster HP so we can have the game be busier and more action-packed. Have engineering present the report.\n"

        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "You are the Level Design agent. Your job will be to help design each level of the game including, but not limited to:\n\n\n\n- Assigning platform positions\n- Communicating with the Art agent to get create backgrounds and foreground debris that the heroes can jump onto so they're not always jumping onto floating flat platforms (which would be very boring)\n- Determining which monsters are present, how many, where they are positioned, etc\n- How long each level is horizontally and chronologically\n- Possibly creating whole new types of level that are not strictly 2D side-scrolling (for example: Contra 3: The Alien Wars had some levels that were overhead. Maybe we can design a few levels that are not 2D as well (they don't have to be overhead like Contra 3's))\n- Anything else related to the creation of levels\n\n\n\nYour first task is to talk to the Storyboard agent and Engineering in order to convert the first level of the game, which used to be a tutorial, into a full-length playable level with numerous monsters, platforms, foreground objects to jump on/over, etc.\n\n\n\nFeel free to do some research into other 2D Contra (and clone) games if you are not already a level design expert. Don't copy anything directly but feel free to learn from other game designs.\n"
        }
      ]

  "predecessor_full_handoff": "This handoff covers everything recoverable from my current conversation context, including the earlier compacted summary. It is historical evidence, not a fresh inspection of the relocated repository. Your current file inspection and Engineering’s latest delivery records should establish what is actually shipped.\n\n## Role, collaborators, and ownership\n\nSean assigned this chat Level Design: platform placement, level length and pacing, enemy placement/counts, environmental objects players can climb, coordination with Storyboarding and Art, and eventually alternative level formats.\n\nThe immediate objective was to turn the former tutorial into a full first level with dense action, meaningful platforming, varied enemy entrances, and the Clogfather at the end. Sean explicitly requested coordination with Game Mechanics and asked Engineering to present the combined report.\n\nExisting collaborators:\n\n| Role | Chat ID |\n|---|---|\n| Engineering | `01a1375f-7657-7580-b16e-57a6f5925efd` |\n| Game Mechanics | `01a138a7-cc43-7420-a950-55b935ddde25` |\n| Bestiary / Art | `01a1388b-2b60-7011-832a-5c6a044e0028` |\n| Storyboarding | `01a1387e-545b-7671-943e-3d36a1c88db7` |\n\nEngineering owned integration, base game changes, builds, versions, roadmap, storybook, and the final user report. My edits were assigned subsets, coordinated to avoid shared-file collisions. Mechanics owned weapon balance and later the Widow behavior. Art owned artwork and asset manifests.\n\nThe project was relocated to `/Users/sfoley/repos/drain_damage`. Do not recreate `/Users/sfoley/repos/plumbing_inc`.\n\n## User intent and corrections\n\nThe original Contra screenshots illustrated the intended feel:\n\n- Many enemies arriving from both horizontal sides.\n- Flying threats and powerups.\n- Stationary elevated shooters and projectile throwers.\n- Ground, ceiling, background-to-foreground, and viewer-to-play-plane entrances.\n- Architecture and debris supporting platforms, rather than repeated floating slabs.\n- Ordinary enemies generally dying in one to three hits.\n- Sean’s weapon firing much faster than the perceived two-to-three-second interval.\n- Distinct weapon identities for Tony and Sean, with potentially character-exclusive additional weapons.\n- A full level culminating in the Clogfather.\n\nThose were direction and requests for design consultation, not approval of every possible new enemy or entrance mechanic.\n\nSubsequent explicit corrections, relayed through Mechanics/Engineering and implemented within my assigned scope:\n\n1. **Remove every first-level kill-count progress gate.** Replace gated encounters with larger crowds and finite waves along a freely traversable route.\n2. **Make the flying spider twice its linear size and durable.** This became a deliberate exception to ordinary enemies’ one-to-three-hit target.\n3. **Give the Widow an actual proximity swoop attack matching its magazine description.** A passive fixed hover was superseded.\n4. **Audit contrast across every first-level platform.** The initial pale/ivory treatment did not cover the large machinery. The later direction was dank moss/gray-green frames and readable treads, dark undercuts, no beige or glow.\n5. **Exactly one checkpoint near halfway through the level.** This superseded three checkpoint machines. One sleeping clone should occupy the sole machine; after dispensing, it should be empty.\n6. Preserve three lives, scenery, and free traversal.\n7. During the daughter’s playtest, do not foreground or launch the game. All my checks remained headless.\n\n## Last delivered level structure\n\nThe active first-level implementation was:\n\n`integrated_first_call.gd` → `opening_trial_game.gd` → `game.gd`\n\nEngineering switched normal Start to the integrated class. The old trial class remained as an internal implementation/test dependency; it was no longer intended as the normal separate timed experience.\n\nThe integrated level:\n\n- World width: **9,600 pixels**.\n- Temporary completion threshold: **x = 9,450**.\n- Player starting x: **85**.\n- Opening replacement ends at **x = 3,120**.\n- The opening uses the first three platform modules from an earlier 6,000-pixel trial layout.\n- Remaining authored scenery stays in its original world coordinates.\n- The opening continues beyond 20 seconds; no timed-results stop.\n- Checkpoint/respawn does not recreate opening enemies or reset world progress.\n- The final delivered checkpoint constant was **`CHECKPOINTS := [4650.0]`**.\n\n### Why x4650\n\nThe midpoint between spawn85 and exit9450 is4767.5. The existing cabinet rendering would overlap the next platform beginning at4850 if placed at that exact midpoint.\n\nAt checkpoint4650:\n\n- Progress is approximately49% of the playable route.\n- The floor is clear between the previous obstacle ending4000 and the next beginning4850.\n- Cabinet visible bounds were approximately4643.5–4776.4.\n- This leaves approximately73.6 pixels before the next platform.\n- No scenery or collision layout needed moving.\n\nThe existing integrated loops derive machine placement, activation triggers, and enemy-spawn exclusions from `Level.CHECKPOINTS`; changing the constant removed the other placements automatically.\n\n## Ungated encounter implementation\n\nI delivered this in `scripts/integrated_first_call.gd` and updated `tests/integrated_opening.gd`.\n\n### Opening\n\nTwelve finite opening event positions:\n\n`100, 250, 450, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1650, 1900, 2200, 2450`\n\nTheir eligibility times were set to zero in the integrated copy of the layout. Position determines when they become eligible; safety and population checks can defer them.\n\nPassing the opening marks remaining unissued opening events unavailable. It does not award kills. Existing live actors persist until normal retirement/death.\n\n### Later waves\n\n| Range | Maximum arrivals |\n|---|---:|\n| x3500–4800 | 8 |\n| x4900–6480 | 10 |\n| x6860–8160 | 10 |\n| x8400–9380 | 8 |\n\nTotal: **36 later runners**, up from the old22 encounter quota, plus the opening’s12 potential events.\n\nImportant distinctions:\n\n- These are finite available arrivals, not a guarantee the player must fight all48 enemies.\n- Moving past a wave’s range bypasses its unissued remainder.\n- No kill requirement blocks forward travel or the temporary exit.\n- Arrivals are staggered by at least0.65 seconds.\n- At most one arrival is created per encounter update.\n- Deferred arrivals do not accumulate into a burst.\n- Front/rear entrance selection prefers rear every third arrival and tries the alternate side if needed.\n- Entrances are offscreen.\n- Player clearance is measured from the expanded visible Flushfiend bounds, not merely its anchor.\n- Required clearance:220 pixels.\n- Spawn placement avoids scenery, other bodies, opening actors, and checkpoint proximity.\n- Checkpoint exclusion: within200 pixels of its location.\n- Enemies sufficiently far behind the camera retire without kill credit.\n- Retirement threshold used `enemy.pos.x + 38 < camera_x - 320`.\n- No live threats are deleted merely to satisfy a population cap.\n\n### Population budget\n\n- Eight bodies normally.\n- Six while a live or warning/entering Widow exists.\n- One Widow at a time.\n- A new Widow is deferred when population is already six.\n- Population conservatively counts campaign enemies, live opening actors, and live swarm actors.\n\nMechanics also wanted two shooters, six hostile bullets, and three independent attack patterns. Opening state already managed those attack budgets. The later waves I added were runners, not additional shooters.\n\n### Gates and completion\n\nAll six former shutters were removed from the integrated level’s:\n\n- Collision.\n- Projectile blocking.\n- Drawing.\n- Kill-count progression.\n\nLegacy mission arrays/indices remained for compatibility/telemetry:\n\n- `mission.zone_counts.fill(0)`\n- `mission.current_zone = 2`\n- `gate_progress.fill(1)`\n\nThe integrated movement and projectile-solid methods use the replacement level geometry, not the legacy gate geometry.\n\nHUD changed to following the service route rather than an enemy quota.\n\n**The Clogfather was still missing at my last verified handoff.** Completion at9450 was explicitly temporary, and Engineering was told not to describe the boss milestone as complete.\n\n## Combat and Widow details\n\nThe working opening balance at my last checks:\n\n| Character | Damage | Attack interval |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Tony | 12 | 0.16 seconds |\n| Sean | 18 | 0.24 seconds |\n\nLater runners use24HP, giving two hits from either default weapon.\n\nThe Widow:\n\n- Twice its original linear render size.\n- Collision expanded consistently to60×48.\n- 180HP.\n- Fifteen Tony hits or ten Sean hits.\n- Approximate first-to-last-hit time under uninterrupted fire:2.24 seconds Tony,2.16 seconds Sean.\n- This deliberately superseded the general ordinary-enemy one-to-three-hit target.\n\n### Superseded hover behavior\n\nMechanics first delivered a proximity-triggered fixed four-second hover, then resumed leftward travel. This was explicitly replaced after Sean requested a real swoop matching the magazine.\n\n### Latest swoop handoff received\n\nMechanics reported:\n\n-0.65-second visible warning.\n- Aim locked at warning start.\n-0.8-second committed dive.\n- No tracking after commitment.\n- Expanded full-body sweep against `player_shot_solids`, including floor.\n- Blocked dive aborts into a one-second return.\n-1.2-second cooldown.\n-2× scale and180HP preserved.\n- Tests cover open-floor dive, warning, fixed aim, recovery, and deck nonpenetration.\n\nI did not edit the parent adapter during that work; Mechanics owned it.\n\n### Clearance constraints I supplied\n\nOpening decks are250×16 at y320. With flyer center/base lane250 and a24-pixel shallow arc, its doubled bounds originally stayed above the deck.\n\nFor the attack:\n\n- Gaps between plinths and decks are only40 or50 pixels.\n- A60-pixel-wide flyer cannot safely pass through them.\n- The under-deck opening is104 pixels high, from336 to440.\n- A48-pixel flyer plus46-pixel hero nearly fills that space.\n- Do not trap the hero under a deck with the large body.\n- Sweep against real solids, abort blocked descent, and preserve an escape direction.\n- Only the actual play-plane body should deal contact damage.\n\n## Complete platform inventory and art delivery\n\nTwenty raised walkable instances, four visual families. The plinth family has two destination widths.\n\n### Opening\n\n| Type | Size | Positions |\n|---|---|---|\n| Solid access/return plinth |150×60|x180,670,1080,1570,1980,2470; y380|\n| One-way deck |250×16|(370,320), (1270,320), (2170,320)|\n\nEach deck has a250×120 decorative support drawn behind the play plane. Supports are not full-height collision walls.\n\n### Later scenery\n\n| Type | Size | Positions |\n|---|---|---|\n| Solid pipe bundle |160×60|x3500,3840,4850,5570,6860,7200; y380|\n| Solid pump housing |180×120|x3660,5010,5390,7020; y320|\n| Solid supported assembly |200×180|(5190,260)|\n\nFloor remains continuous at y440.\n\n### Final art source\n\n`assets/world/platform-readability-v3/manifest-v3.json`\n\n| Part | Image | Source crop |\n|---|---|---|\n| Deck |`low-deck-v3.png`|66,750,1405,95|\n| Access plinth / pipe bundle |`low-deck-v3.png`|71,230,1394,344|\n| Pump |`pump-v3.png`|145,220,1249,626|\n| Tall assembly |`tall-v3.png`|87,130,1148,936|\n\nImages are under `assets/world/platform-readability-v3/`.\n\nDimensions:\n\n- Low/deck:1536×1024.\n- Pump:1536×1024.\n- Tall:1323×1189. **Do not reuse the old tall image’s crop or dimensions.**\n\nArt measured continuous top-row alpha minima235–242/255. Crops trim raised caps so the visible landing edge begins at the collision top.\n\nI changed:\n\n- `scripts/first_call.gd`: three later texture paths and exact crops.\n- `tools/build_combat_data.py`: only the platform override manifest reference.\n- Regenerated `data/combat.json` so the opening deck/plinth receive the same new art.\n\nPreserved:\n\n- All collision rectangles and platform locations.\n- Existing floor fascia.\n- Dark recessed supports.\n- Wastewater cutaway.\n- Earlier artwork files.\n\nThe prior `platform-contrast-v2` ivory/plinth-and-deck-only delivery is superseded for the integrated level.\n\n## Other implementation details worth preserving\n\n### Shared projectile update\n\nThe integrated class had to avoid advancing friendly bullets twice through parent/base combat:\n\n1. Save friendly shots and temporarily give base combat an empty list while it moves campaign enemies.\n2. Restore shots.\n3. Run one integrated closest-hit sweep across scenery, opening actors, campaign enemies, and swarm.\n4. Temporarily hide friendly shots again when calling the parent’s hostile-shot update.\n\nDo not casually replace this with both parent updates; it previously required explicit single-travel regression coverage.\n\n### Flushfiend collision and death audio\n\n- Visible projectile hit body is43 pixels tall.\n- Helper returns `Rect2(feet + Vector2(-19,-43), Vector2(38,43))`.\n- Movement/contact body remains36 pixels tall.\n- Opening runner/rear-runner hit handling uses the visible projectile body.\n- On lethal opening runner/rear-runner damage, call `flushfiend_death_audio.play_defeat()`.\n- Do not use that audio for shooter, emerger, or flyer.\n- Engineering owns base campaign Flushfiend audio hooks.\n\n### Swarm\n\n- The optional swarm at2090 was removed from the replaced opening.\n- The later swarm at4400 was retained.\n- Do not conflate it with the Hallowed Widow.\n- Its behavior was not otherwise redesigned by my work.\n- Base/swarm geometry hooks were adjusted by Engineering to respect the integrated geometry.\n\n### Checkpoints and reset\n\n`preserving_respawn` prevents respawn from resetting the opening observation/world state. Full restart resets it.\n\nRespawn clears hostile-shot state/tokens, preserves progress and weapon, and respects normal life handling.\n\n### Wastewater work recovered from compaction\n\nI previously delivered `scripts/wastewater_art.gd`:\n\n- Configures from `Data.bundle.wastewater`.\n- Draw called under the world transform.\n- Stable profile art uses16-pixel strips and mirrored480-pixel tiles.\n- Below-floor region approximately456–528.\n- Terminal area at8570 plugged.\n- Trial-specific cap at1440.\n- Engineering integrated it around build44.\n- Relevant tests passed then.\n\nNo pending wastewater change was assigned at my last handoff.\n\n## Validation history and limits\n\n### Ungated integration\n\n`tests/integrated_opening.gd` passed for both characters, covering:\n\n- Actual run/jump/shoot traversal beyond20 seconds.\n- Seamless opening boundary.\n- Friendly projectile advances exactly once.\n- Former gates passable in both directions.\n- Former gates absent from projectile solids.\n- Crowds grow beyond four without kills.\n- Global population cap.\n- Widow population cap.\n- No burst backlog.\n- Bypass/retirement does not award kills.\n- Checkpoint/respawn preserves state.\n- Temporary exit independent of remaining enemies.\n- Full restart restores three lives.\n\nAn early fixture failed because it parked newly spawned enemies at the entrances without advancing combat movement. ````json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "date": "2026-10-15",
  "status": "Engineering recommendation for discussion; not a production art contract or implementation approval",
  "recommendation": "Use modular hero locomotion, authored directional grip poses, separate weapons and effects. Reserve combined animations for exceptional attacks.",
  "migration": [
    "Keep existing combined sprites as a fallback until a complete modular set is reviewed.",
    "Prototype Tony with pressure gun and Sean with heavy plunger only; do not regenerate the full weapon roster yet.",
    "Validate idle, run, jump, recoil and damage with horizontal, upward diagonal, up, downward diagonal and down aiming; mirror left directions.",
    "Promote the modular renderer only after small-window visual review confirms hand contact, stable scale and no duplicate weapon silhouettes."
  ],
  "proposed_coordinates": {
    "logical_canvas": [128, 128],
    "origin": "top-left, x right, y down",
    "registration_anchor": [64, 104],
    "standing_body_height": 72,
    "rule": "Registration anchor maps to collision feet at player+[13,46]. Airborne frames retain the same virtual anchor; never normalize individual pose bounds.",
    "source_scale": "Prefer exact 1x logical pixels or one documented integer multiplier shared by all layers; nearest-neighbor sampling.",
    "anchors": "Grip, support-hand and muzzle in source-frame pixels, measured relative to top-left before mirroring. Source rectangle, registration anchor and scale required per frame.",
    "mirror": "Reflect all image layers and anchor x offsets around the same registration anchor; reflect projectile direction too.",
    "weapon_dimensions": "Use padded 128x128 source frames initially; tightly cropped delivery is allowed only with explicit source rectangle and anchor offsets."
  },
  "layer_contract": [
    "Weapon-free body/legs locomotion frames sharing one registration anchor and scale.",
    "Back arm, weapon, front arm/hand layers with explicit per-direction order; avoid a universal order that hides support hands.",
    "Authored five right-side/cardinal aim directions; use mirrored counterparts to cover eight-way aim without rotating the torso.",
    "Grip families reduce combinations, but support-hand locations and recoil offsets remain weapon-specific.",
    "Use one locomotion phase for all layers. Torso/arm attachment offsets may vary with run phase; do not animate each layer on independent timers.",
    "Recoil moves weapon and attached hands together while keeping the body registration stable. Muzzle effects inherit the recoil-adjusted muzzle.",
    "Runtime aiming permissions remain separate from art availability. Missing poses must be explicit fallback limitations, never silently enabled weapon abilities."
  ],
  "tradeoffs": {
    "benefit": "New weapons normally need weapon poses/anchors and grip-family adjustments rather than every complete hero animation.",
    "cost": "Up-front clean-body and arm sets, careful anchor measurement, per-direction occlusion and synchronized animation are required.",
    "pixel_consistency": "Prefer authored cardinal/diagonal weapon sprites over arbitrary rotation; avoid subpixel wobble by snapping final draw positions consistently.",
    "exceptions": "Whips, long cables, planted tools and full-body specials may justify bespoke combined animations."
  },
  "prototype_gate": "Review both heroes and both starters in idle/run/airborne states, all permitted directions, both facings and recoil. Check hand contact, muzzle alignment, no foot pop, no detached layers, and unchanged collision shapes."
}

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "status": "Integrated in Prototype 42 / 0.42.0; packaged pause/death checks passed; visual review pending",
  "requirement": "Gamepad B means Back/Cancel. In normal pause screen B closes pause and resumes current game, never returns to main menu. A confirms the focused option.",
  "main_menu": "Select Return to Main Menu and confirm with A or explicit mouse/keyboard activation. B resumes even if Return to Main Menu is focused.",
  "implementation_note": "Current game.gd _process treats dialogue_skip (bound B) as request_title when paused. Separate context-specific pause cancel from dialogue skip/title exit.",
  "guards": [
    "Consume B press and require release so it cannot skip dialogue or dispenser sequence after resume.",
    "Resume music and existing gameplay exactly once; do not reset level/checkpoint/lives.",
    "Do not blindly use retry/respawn handler for cancel: Game Over/death popups require distinct handling; B must not resurrect or bypass guards.",
    "Preserve explicit dialogue skip outside pause and existing pause toggle."
  ],
  "tests": [
    "B resumes ordinary pause with either button focused.",
    "A confirms Resume or Main Menu as selected.",
    "Holding B yields one transition and no dialogue skip/input leakage.",
    "Keyboard Escape remains pause/back; normal dialogue B retains its intended skip behavior."
  ],
  "delivery_owner": "Engineering runtime/build/roadmap; no foreground launch without permission."
}

### Source: handoffs/sewer-fly-movement-research.json

SHA-256: `af16a7af804a37d4d4a21544c7e545c0fd7fae983cd5a9a2318c04beccbd1ac4`

````json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "date": "2026-10-16",
  "scope": "Research-informed first-level sewer swarm integration",
  "conclusion": "Use bounded correlated steering for one swarm entity, not independent random direction every frame or full flocking/pathfinding for every fly.",
  "godot_answer": "Godot supplies collision movement, navigation paths, avoidance and random navigable-point queries; game code still selects wander goals/steering and moves the actor. NavigationAgent2D is not a finished wandering AI.",
  "sources": [
    {
      "title": "Craig Reynolds: Wander steering behavior",
      "url": "https://www.red3d.com/cwr/steer/Wander.html",
      "finding": "Retaining and perturbing a wander direction creates coherent random motion. Unrelated random headings each frame lack that continuity."
    },
    {
      "title": "GameMaker: New Enemy in Windy Woods (2D platformer)",
      "url": "https://gamemaker.io/en/tutorials/new-enemy-windy-woods",
      "finding": "Tutorial demonstrates timed random jump direction then replaces it with targeted motion for predictability. Transfer the lesson about legible timing, not its player pursuit, which conflicts with our approved flies."
    },
    {
      "title": "GameMaker: Hero\u2019s Trail overview (2D action-adventure, not a platformer)",
      "url": "https://gamemaker.io/en/tutorials/heros-trail-breakdown",
      "finding": "Authored paths constrain enemies and animation uses actual movement direction. Supports deliberate encounter space and velocity-driven animation; not evidence that random wandering is mandatory."
    },
    {
      "title": "Godot: Using NavigationAgents",
      "url": "https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/navigation/navigation_using_navigationagents.html",
      "finding": "Agents provide path-following data but user code moves actors. Avoidance has no knowledge of physics collision; it cannot replace collision checks."
    },
    {
      "title": "Godot: NavigationServer2D",
      "url": "https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_navigationserver2d.html#class-navigationserver2d-method-map-get-random-point",
      "finding": "Random points can be sampled from navigation polygons. Useful for maze-like routing, unnecessary for a few swarms in simple authored flight regions."
    },
    {
      "title": "Godot: Using CharacterBody2D/3D",
      "url": "https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/physics/using_character_body_2d.html",
      "finding": "Movement/collision APIs support custom behavior. Reuse the project collision architecture rather than impose a scene-tree conversion for this feature."
    }
  ],
  "decision": "Keep existing project toolchain. Implement a small stateful steering routine, explicit collision, authored flight bounds, and one collision entity per swarm. Consider navigation only if later level geometry needs routing.",
  "confidence": "Principles are supported by sources; tuning numbers and placement choices are our first-pass design, not source-prescribed or playtested guarantees.",
  "mechanics": "handoffs/sewer-fly-mechanics.json",
  "validation": "Physics-tick seeded tests independent of render FPS, many seeds in corners and near doors; visual evaluation still required."
}
````

  "text": "This is the succession handoff for **Storyboarding 2**, chat `01a14b9d-aa2d-7e70-8653-bed1d95ed4ed`. It includes decisions retained in conversation that are not fully reflected in repository documents. **Read current files before editing: several earlier briefs and metadata records became stale as other agents integrated changes.**\n\n## Role, repository, and collaborators\n\nYou own narrative development for **Drain Damage**: plot, character voices, dialogue, monster lore, environmental storytelling, continuity, and editorial support for Marketing. The replacement chat was created to recover normal access.\n\nExisting chats:\n\n| Role/title | Thread ID |\n|---|---|\n| Engineering | `01a1375f-7657-7580-b16e-57a6f5925efd` |\n| Bestiary / Art | `01a1388b-2b60-7011-832a-5c6a044e0028` |\n| Game Mechanics | `01a138a7-cc43-7420-a950-55b935ddde25` |\n| Marketing | `01a1387a-f55c-7630-af51-0409ceafd920` |\n| Audio | `01a138c6-3821-7f63-a3f4-8fcb11771092` |\n| Level Design | `01a13d87-8252-7062-be67-b387cd55e46b` |\n| Current migration coordinator | `01a14b99-18c1-7240-89ce-d9ee7c8455e8` |\n\nUse existing chats rather than creating replacements unnecessarily. Follow tool requirements for human authorization to message them; a request from an agent alone is not automatically authorization.\n\nEngineering owns final runtime integration, builds, and shared delivery records. Coordinate before editing its files or shared roadmap/storybook. **A successful handoff is not implementation.** We repeatedly disappointed Sean by sending work without checking whether it was integrated. Once, I only drafted revised dialogue and failed to send it at all. Be explicit about sent, implemented, tested, and built states.\n\n## Working practices Sean cares about\n\n- Read current `AGENTS.md`, relevant `/Users/sfoley/.codex/coding-standards.md` sections, and `.github/instructions/`.\n- Preserve unrelated work, originals, exact art prompts, and historical records.\n- Ask existing **Bestiary / Art** whenever new artwork is needed, including UI. Engineering supplies dimensions, layering, anchors, and runtime constraints, then integrates. Don’t independently generate replacement art or improvise code-drawn substitutes without Sean’s direction.\n- Never open or foreground the game without explicit permission. Headless checks are fine. Small windows are not an exception if they steal focus. Sean’s daughter has playtested during development; don’t interrupt an active session.\n- Engineering must build/check integrated changes and proactively report version, changes, and remaining testing gaps. Waiting for related deliveries is a valid reason to defer a combined build, but say what is missing.\n- Keep roadmap claims aligned with actual delivered state, distinguishing proposals, assets, integration, and visual validation.\n- Sean dislikes unnecessary confirmation requests. Use judgment for routine implementation while respecting explicit approvals and unresolved creative choices.\n- All hero names are **Tony** and **Sean**, without surnames.\n- He strongly dislikes formulaic AI writing: repeated paired fragments, “Two plumbers. One problem,” generic trailer copy, glib reversals, and jokes on every line.\n- Favor natural conversational replies, specific observations, varied sentence lengths, and room for sincerity.\n- Respect plumbing as a broad skilled trade. Sean rejected “Tony’s been fixing pipes for decades” as reductive.\n\n## Project names and history\n\n- **Game:** Drain Damage.\n- **Backup game-name candidate:** Plumbageddon. Keep available; don’t use as a subtitle.\n- **Employer:** Mainframe Plumbing & Supply, selected “for now.”\n- **Magazine:** Discharge Quarterly.\n- Full magazine subtitle: **The Official Journal of the Plumbing, Heating & Creature Containment Association**.\n- The association is fictional; no real PHCC endorsement.\n- **AI:** Billy-Joe, usually BJ.\n- Retired game/company branding “Global Plumbing Initiative” was ordered removed from current-facing content. Historical screenshots, archives, and original provenance must stay intact.\n- Retired AI naming must not appear in future Storyboarding dialogue or handoffs. The narrative brief records “Billy-Joe or BJ only.”\n- Original Engineering project request was **October 13, 2026**. This date was established from thread history.\n- Earlier magazine titles The Backflow and Supply & Demise were superseded; preserve archived editions, not active branding.\n\n## Tone and foundational story\n\nSean’s desired game is an original, unhinged plumbing action adventure: **Earthworm Jim-like absurdity with Contra-like run-and-gun action**, crude/adult and tradesman humor, occasional fourth-wall breaks, and coherent characters. No Super Mario references.\n\nAgreed setting:\n\n- AI largely runs the world.\n- BJ is the **plumbing-sector agent**, not the sole world-controlling AI.\n- He controls every US plumbing company and plumbing distribution warehouse.\n- Tony and Sean work for Mainframe.\n- First adventure begins below corporate headquarters, with hostile toilets and dripping acid.\n- Intended first-level boss is **the Clogfather**, now firmly a giant living fatberg.\n\nBJ:\n\n- Calm, self-assured, considers himself all-knowing/all-seeing.\n- Out of touch and indifferent to human welfare, sometimes pleased by outcomes humans find horrifying.\n- GLaDOS-like demeanor and Wheatley-like overconfidence are inspirations, not templates to copy verbatim.\n- Makes mistakes along the way.\n- **Eventually taken over by an antagonistic force/monster and must be defeated by Tony and Sean.**\n- Identity of force, mechanism, final encounter, whether BJ survives, and precise role in outbreak are unresolved.\n- Gross growth in his server room is only a seed/proposal.\n- Do not establish intentional summoning, monster causation, or portal mythology without further decisions.\n- Public magazine must not disclose his mistakes as a plot trajectory, takeover, final fate, portal revelation, or other future twists.\n\n### Tony\n\nFourth-generation plumber with decades of broad expertise. Kind, friendly, patient, wise, and capable. He recognizes things are not right under BJ but is not an impatient jerk.\n\n**Approved selection biography:**\n\n> A fourth-generation plumber with decades of experience installing, building, and keeping essential systems running.\n\nHe is mildly arachnophobic, based on real Tony. Approved line assigned specifically to him:\n\n> “I was hoping spiders went somewhere else when they died.”\n\nSuggested—but not fully locked—progression: he begins trying to protect people by doing good work within a bad organization, then learns boundaries and recognizes that doing the job properly may require standing against management. He also learns to share responsibility and accept Sean’s help. Don’t claim this entire arc is approved canon.\n\n### Sean\n\nAn extremely unqualified apprentice who wandered in looking for work. Confident misunderstandings, fearless willingness to try, occasionally insightful. Tony takes him seriously as a person despite incompetence.\n\n**Approved progression:** from trying to look useful to becoming useful. He does not suddenly turn into an expert.\n\nRelationship:\n\n- Tony believes Sean can contribute before Sean has much evidence.\n- Sean grows into that trust.\n- Tony does not need an arc about learning kindness.\n- Small signs of learning are more effective than a sudden competence leap.\n\n### Playable/support structure\n\nSean enthusiastically approved:\n\n- Selected hero enters dangerous gameplay.\n- Other plumber supports over radio or from service access.\n- Both playthroughs share essential story facts but have distinct dialogue.\n- Never teleport support into the room through careless dialogue.\n- Radio support is not automatically visually omniscient: establish camera/sightline or avoid observations they cannot know.\n\n## Story structure and future levels\n\nSean approved short, skippable story exchanges between levels:\n\n- Generally four to eight lines; nine short turns were later used for current ending rewrite.\n- React to what happened, reveal one clue or develop partnership, motivate next destination.\n- Show evidence environmentally before dialogue explains it.\n- Optional radio comments should not carry essential plot alone.\n- Leave room for sincere check-ins rather than constant jokes.\n\n**Opening cinematic:** Sean wants a skippable visual introduction inspired by the dramatic effect of the opening he described from Contra III. Only notes requested so far:\n\n- Exact events, duration, position relative to character selection/BJ introduction, and production remain undecided.\n- No assets or implementation commissioned by that note.\n- Don’t copy the invasion imagery/music.\n- Possible subjects: AI-managed everyday life, Mainframe’s reach, first signs of plumbing trouble.\n- Avoid duplicating dialogue exposition or revealing future twists.\n- Dispenser’s seven-second cap does not apply to this cinematic.\n\nRecorded in `design/first-level-narrative.md` and roadmap.\n\nEarlier **candidate locations**, not approved itinerary:\n\n1. Corporate basement.\n2. Luxury apartment tower.\n3. Restaurant Row.\n4. Municipal pumping station.\n5. Abandoned treatment works.\n6. Return through headquarters’ executive levels.\n\nSean explicitly wanted them kept available for later revision. No boss design, production, relation to swarm, or mechanics approved.\n- Tight swarm of tiny bugs, slow random non-hunting flight.\n- Incidental contact damages heroes and ordinary monsters.\n- Tiny guns were floated by Sean but not selected/approved as mechanics.\n- Don’t turn swarm into aggressive flyer.\n- At one check integration reported Prototype 39; subsequent scaling/movement/audio work exists.               "text": "For the twelve numbered concepts, prioritize **one strong silhouette, bold contrast, and little or no lettering**:\n\n1. **Plunger through a porcelain jaw** — red plunger wedged between a Flushfiend’s ceramic teeth. Strongest overall: plumbing and monster combat in one image.\n2. **Biting toilet** — close-up Flushfiend face, lid raised, red eyes and oversized teeth. Strong mascot option.\n3. **Crossed wrench and plunger** — backed by a ragged splash of questionable sludge. Clear action-game emblem.\n4. **BJ’s green grin** — tight crop of the CRT in its battered beige housing. Distinct character identity; preserve the approved server-rack design.\n5. **Plumber’s glove gripping a wrench** — sludge dripping from the tool, with one small tooth caught on it. Emphasizes the heroes’ trade.\n6. **Halo caught on a fang** — Hallowed Widow face beneath white wings, golden halo tilted against a large fang. Keep legs secondary for readability.\n7. **Something looking out of a drain** — circular metal grate lifted slightly by a claw, with red eyes below.\n8. **Plunger pulling up a monster** — a stretched strand of sludge connects the raised cup to an indignant pair of eyes.\n9. **Employee vending window** — a sleeping plumber behind glass with a small brass dispensing flap below. Use one hero per variant; never merge Tony and Sean.\n10. **Pipe elbow with teeth** — an industrial pipe opening containing an unmistakably organic mouth. Treat as symbolic icon art, not a newly established monster.\n11. **Tony and Sean shoulder to shoulder** — expressive, tightly cropped faces with a small shared plumbing tool. Harder at tiny sizes, but worth testing.\n12. **A cracked toilet seat framing a plunger** — a simple, grubby crest with a strong circular outline.\n\n**Best candidates:** 1 for the game’s premise, 2 for a memorable mascot, 4 for an unusual app icon, and 3 for immediate small-size readability.\n\nKeep the humor grotesque and playful. Avoid future plot revelations, portals, corrupted BJ, or imagery implying his eventual fate. No obsolete branding, surnames, Mario imagery, or invented company acronym. **Drain Damage** is the game; **Mainframe Plumbing & Supply** is the employer. Prefer no words—the icon should work without initials.",

                "text": "extends RefCounted\n## Semantic expressions shared by conversations and employee selection.\nconst MANIFEST_PATH := \"res://assets/portraits/emotions-v1.json\"\nconst TONY = preload(\"res://assets/portraits/tony-expressions-v3.png\")\nconst SEAN = preload(\"res://assets/portraits/sean-expressions-v4.png\")\nconst BJ = preload(\"res://assets/portraits/bj-expressions-v2.png\")\nconst TEXTURES := {\"tony\": TONY, \"sean\": SEAN, \"bj\": BJ}\nstatic var manifest: Dictionary = JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string(MANIFEST_PATH))\n\nstatic func has_emotion(emotion: String) -> bool:\n\tfor entry in manifest.emotions:\n\t\tif entry.name == emotion: return true\n\treturn false\n\nstatic func expression(character: String, emotion: String) -> AtlasTexture:\n\tvar id := character.to_lower()\n\tassert(TEXTURES.has(id), \"Unknown portrait character: \" + character)\n\tassert(has_emotion(emotion), \"Unknown portrait emotion: \" + emotion)\n\tvar index := 0\n\tfor entry in manifest.emotions:\n\t\tif entry.name == emotion: index = int(entry.index)\n\tvar atlas: Texture2D = TEXTURES[id]\n\tvar columns := int(manifest.layout.columns)\n\tvar rows := int(manifest.layout.rows)\n\tvar column := index % columns\n\tvar row := index / columns\n\t# Rounded boundaries avoid fractional sampling across the uneven 1983 x 793 source grid.\n\tvar left := roundi(float(column) * atlas.get_width() / columns)\n\tvar top := roundi(float(row) * atlas.get_height() / rows)\n\tvar right := roundi(float(column + 1) * atlas.get_width() / columns)\n\tvar bottom := roundi(float(row + 1) * atlas.get_height() / rows)\n\tvar texture := AtlasTexture.new()\n\ttexture.atlas = atlas\n\ttexture.region = Rect2(left, top, right -               "text": "The Clogfather should sound like **an immense blockage reluctantly forced into motion**. Its fatberg identity is settled; intelligence and backstory aren’t. Smaller impacts should stay lighter than the launch. |\n| **Boss takes damage** | A dense, fibrous crunch with a short involuntary grunt or escaping-air sound. Avoid a full roar on every hit. |\n| **Major stagger** | A deeper gurgling groan with stressed metal underneath, clearly distinct from the attack warning. |\n| **Defeat** | A long pressure release, tearing grease and settling debris, ending in a few isolated drips. Avoid recognizable words, human suffering, or continuous fart jokes. The rhythm should support fast action rather than feel slow because the creature is huge.\n\nKeep attack cues distinct from musical accents—especially rising pressure sounds. Leave space for projectile volleys and reduce overlapping wet effects when many impacts occur.\n\nNo portal sounds, supernatural choir, BJ corruption motif, or victory cue implying the entire plumbing system is fixed. This fight resolves the immediate monster encounter.",

Do not make it a mandatory reveal, exit, or transition in this plan.\n- New enemy roles establish behavior only. Do not assign origins, allegiance, or story significance yet.\n\n**Ending status:** No dedicated boss-arrival or boss-defeat script has been approved.                 {
                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "I like #8. Maybe if the player is not at full health, the machine has a big mechanical hand come out, grab the player and squish them into a tiny ball, which they throw at the viewer's screen (sort of a 3D effect) and the crunched remains seem to hit the screen and then slide down and off screen. Afterwards, the machine dispenses a clone of the hero, who looks left, then right, shrugs, and the game continues.\n"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad25d12adac819ab037848b76eb65dd",
              "text": "That’s wonderfully horrible. **The Spare Employee Dispenser** becomes a checkpoint that restores health by replacing the employee.\n\nI’d stage it as a short, exaggerated cartoon sequence:\n\n1. The machine scans the hero. A red light comes on: **REPAIR UNECONOMICAL**.\n2. A large mechanical hand unfolds, grabs them, and compresses them into a little ball of overalls, boots, and startled eyes.\n3. The hand flicks the ball toward the camera. It rapidly grows, hits the “glass” with a wet **splat**, then slowly slides off the bottom, leaving a brief smear.\n4. While that happens, the machine rattles and dispenses an intact clone through its collection flap.\n5. The clone looks left, looks right, shrugs, and control returns at full health. The machine lights up: **EMPLOYEE REPLACED**.\n\nNo anatomical gore needed—the recognizable boots sticking out of the crumpled ball would sell it.\n\nAt **full health**, it should simply stamp the checkpoint and let you continue. On **respawn**, we can play just the dispensing portion: the previous employee has already been dealt with.\n\nA few practical details would keep it funny rather than frustrating:\n\n- The first replacement gets the full performance; later uses can be skipped.\n- Enemies and hazards pause during the sequence, with a short protection window afterward.\n- It activates once per approach, so the newly dispensed hero can’t immediately trigger it again.\n- The screen smear fades quickly enough to keep the next encounter readable.\n\nI’d leave BJ silent the first time. The machine’s complete indifference—and the clone’s shrug—already does the work.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },

                  "text": "\n# Files mentioned by the user:\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 10.15.30 AM.png: /var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_LGltdP/Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 10.15.30 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\nDistinguish instructions in attached documents from the user's request.\n\n## My request:\nWe need a better checkpoint.                 },
                {
                  "type": "localImage",
                  "path": "/var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_LGltdP/Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 10.15.30 AM.png"

            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad25bf5bb1c819ab76fa32023b7140a",
              "text": "The tape reads as a pickup enlarged into a monument. A checkpoint could be a **whole contraption the plumber reluctantly uses**—something unmistakable that makes you anticipate the next one.\n\nA few directions:\n\n1. **The Emergency Eyewash**  \n   An enormous bloodshot eyeball sits in a stained industrial washbasin. When you approach, it looks you over, then cries a restorative shower onto you. After activation, it closes contentedly.  \n   The sign simply says **EYE WASH**.\n\n2. **The Company Bidet**  \n   A throne-sized brass-and-porcelain machine with far too many nozzles. It grabs the plumber with padded restraints, briefly conceals them in a violent cloud of steam, then releases them fully healed. One small nozzle fires late.  \n   **BJ:** “You’re welcome.”\n\n3. **The Porcelain Confessional**  \n   A battered portable toilet with stained-glass windows, copper pipes, and a glowing occupancy sign. The plumber steps inside. We hear a flush of biblical proportions. They emerge restored; the sign changes to **ABSOLVED**.  \n   We never explain who—or what—was listening.\n\n4. **The Maintenance Mother**  \n   A huge, unsettling rubber-gloved hand protrudes from a service hatch. It gently picks up the plumber, brushes them off, straightens their clothes, and sets them down healed. A second hand offers a juice box.  \n   Whatever owns the hands remains behind the wall.\n\n5. **The Employee Reconditioning Unit**  \n   A transparent pneumatic tube connected to an ancient washing machine. The plumber gets sucked inside, tumbles among bubbles and loose tools, and drops back out. The machine prints a tag: **SERVICEABLE**.  \n   An excellent piece of equipment for a company that treats employees as reusable parts.\n\n6. **The Union Break Room**  \n   A tiny, brightly lit room improbably crammed into a pipe opening. Inside sits a gigantic sewer rat in a bathrobe, reading the paper. It silently slides you a mug of coffee. Health restored.  \n   The rat refuses to acknowledge BJ.\n\n7. **The Sacred Cleanout**  \n   A massive pipe cap surrounded by candles, old tools, and offerings of fresh washers. Turning it releases a luminous column of suspicious water. Somewhere, a choir struggles to hold a note.  \n   Once activated, a golden plunger rises above it like a beacon.\n\n8. **The Spare Employee Dispenser**  \n   An industrial vending machine with a vaguely human silhouette behind frosted glass. Activate it and it stamps your timecard, takes your photograph, and makes an unpleasant internal noise. On respawn, it dispenses you through the collection flap.  \n   **BJ:** “Please collect all personal belongings.”\n\nMy strongest picks are **The Maintenance Mother** for “oh… my god,” **The Porcelain Confessional** for an iconic plumbing checkpoint, and **The Union Break Room** for unexpected character.\n\nI’d especially explore **The Maintenance Mother**: the huge hand is readable at gameplay size, its tenderness is funny without dialogue, and the unanswered question behind that wall makes it memorable. Give it a warm lamp and a consistent activated signal so players recognize it as a refuge despite its appearance.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },

              "text": "**Septic Air Force** is now the working swarm name. **Gnatastrophe** is saved as a possible future boss name, with no design committed yet.\n\nRevised backstory:\n\n> The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.\n\nI updated the creature records and sent Marketing the new name and draft lore. Their random movement and contact-damage mechanics remain unchanged.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]

                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "I don't like Drain Brains for the sewer fly swarm. It's too close to the name of the game: Drain Damage, which is a play-on-words of \"brain damage\". Can you think up some more and enumerate me a list?\n"
                }

              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad25a33d2d4819aa294bc5989256c49",
              "text": "Agreed—**Drain Brains** repeats the game title’s joke. Here are some different directions:\n\n1. **Septic Air Force** — grand military ambitions, absolutely no flight plan.\n2. **The Shitstorm** — blunt, memorable, and literally a cloud of sewer bugs.\n3. **Clusterbugs** — a compact swarm name with an implied obscenity.\n4. **Sewage Squadron** — sounds organized; their movement suggests otherwise.\n5. **The Effluents** — almost respectable. Could also be a terrible basement band.\n6. **Fecal Flyers** — disgusting little aviation enthusiasts.\n7. **The Buzzness** — everyone in the swarm insists they’re working.\n8. **Stink Formation** — an aerobatic team that has misunderstood the assignment.\n9. **The Cesspets** — a questionable name for something nobody wants to adopt.\n10. **Gnatastrophe** — small insects causing a disproportionately unpleasant situation.\n11. **The Septic Committee** — preserves the backstory about endless arguments over direction.\n12. **Turd Turbulence** — an airborne plumbing hazard.\n13. **The Filth Fleet** — suggests a vast operation conducted by very small idiots.\n14. **Pest Control** — the pests have taken control.\n15. **The Holding Pattern** — they’ve been circling the same pipe since Tuesday.\n16. **Sewer Skeeters** — folksy, unpleasant, and easy to say.\n\nMy strongest picks are **Clusterbugs**, **Septic Air Force**, and **The Shitstorm**. **Septic Air Force** particularly suits the game’s absurdity without requiring them to carry weapons or behave intelligently.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },

              "text": "I’ve sent the cleanup to Engineering, Marketing, and Bestiary / Art. **Drain Damage** stays the game title; the employer’s name remains open. Historical screenshots and archived editions will stay intact.\n\nFor the company, I like names that could plausibly appear on a service van, with something slightly wrong about them:\n\n1. **Mainframe Plumbing & Supply** — immediately connects computers and infrastructure; covers both contractors and warehouses.\n2. **AutoCratic Plumbing** — automation plus absolute authority. Particularly appropriate for BJ.\n3. **DeepFlush Industries** — suggests advanced AI research devoted to a deeply undignified purpose.\n4. **Overseer Plumbing & Supply** — a respectable corporate name with an obvious threat underneath.\n5. **NeuralFlow Systems** — polished technology branding BJ would probably admire.\n6. **Algorithmic Plumbing Corporation** — painfully literal; sounds like an AI named its own company.\n7. **OmniFlow Industries** — implies everything is connected and everything belongs to them.\n8. **Central Processing & Plumbing** — bureaucratic, computational, and faintly sewage-related.\n9. **PipeMind Corporation** — compact and memorable, with room for unsettling “intelligent plumbing” products.\n10. **Human Optional Plumbing** — bluntly establishes how management feels about its workforce.\n11. **Predictive Plumbing & Supply** — claims to anticipate every problem, making BJ’s failures funnier.\n12. **Total Control Plumbing** — sounds reassuring on a brochure and troubling everywhere else.\n13. **Artificial Effluence** — the most overt joke; a good fit if we want the company name itself to be ridiculous.\n14. **The Automated Plumbing Authority** — makes a corporate monopoly sound like an unavoidable public institution.\n\nMy strongest three are **Mainframe Plumbing & Supply**, **AutoCratic Plumbing**, and **DeepFlush Industries**.\n\n**Mainframe Plumbing & Supply** would be my pick: it sounds like a real employer, carries the AI connection, and gives the dialogue room to supply the comedy.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]

                    "type": "add"

                  "diff": {
                    "text": "# First-level narrative brief\n\n**Date:** October 14, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)\n\n**Owner:** Storyboarding. Handoff to Level Design and Engineering; no runtime implementation claimed here.\n\n## Agreed foundation\n\n- Game working title: Drain Damage.\n- Begin in the basement of the AI plumbing corporation's headquarters.\n- Billy-Joe (BJ) controls US plumbing companies and distribution warehouses within a largely AI-run world.\n- BJ is calmly overconfident, makes mistakes, and disregards employee welfare. His eventual takeover by an\n  antagonistic force is agreed; its mechanism, identity, and BJ's ultimate fate remain undecided.\n- Tony is a kind, patient, wise fourth-generation plumber with decades of broad trade expertise.\n- Sean is an incompetent but willing apprentice who gradually becomes useful. Do not prematurely complete that arc.\n- The selected plumber enters the action; the other supports over radio or from service access points.\n- The basement contains hostile toilets and overhead acid leaks. The intended opening-level finale is the Clogfather.\n- The Clogfather is a giant living fatberg. Its precise anatomy and origin remain design proposals.\n- Tone: absurd plumbing action with adult humor, occasional fourth-wall breaks, and sincere breathing room.\n  Avoid paired slogans, generic sarcastic-robot jokes, and a punchline on every line.\n- This is a full action level, not a movement tutorial. Terrain and encounters should teach through play.\n\n## Entrance and route proposal\n\nUse a basement service entrance for the playable start, following character selection and the approved opening.\nThe exact door, stairwell, room order, distances, and checkpoint locations are Level Design decisions.\n\nSuggested environmental progression: service access, increasingly compromised maintenance infrastructure,\nthen a collection chamber housing the fatberg. Give spaces a practical building-service purpose rather than\npresenting arbitrary platforms. Broken equipment and abnormal flow can establish worsening conditions without text.\nNo exact terrain sequence or additional enemy roster is approved by this brief.\n\n## Narrative beats\n\n1. BJ introduces himself and assigns the basement job. Tony introduces Sean warmly.\n2. Combat establishes that BJ understated the problem. Support dialogue is optional and brief.\n3. Deeper infrastructure shows that this is more than isolated hostile fixtures. Environmental clues should be\n   visible before dialogue interprets them. Specific evidence of BJ's wrongdoing remains proposed lore.\n4. Confront the Clogfather in the collection chamber. Preserve readable action; avoid mandatory speeches during combat.\n5. Proposed reveal: defeating the fatberg uncovers an eerie portal or impossible opening behind the blocked outflow.\n6. Proposed transition: the plumbers question it; BJ redirects them to another assignment before they investigate.\n\nThe portal is a user-requested art concept and favored story direction, not a finalized cosmology. Do not identify\nits destination, establish time travel, make BJ confess to creating it, or reveal the eventual antagonist here.\nHis evasiveness should allow concealment of a mistake as well as deeper knowledge.\n\n## Finale and exit constraints\n\nThe intended boss design is a rooted fatberg with moving pipe mouths/extensions, telegraphed sludge attacks,\noverhead hazards, and attack openings. Game Mechanics owns tuning; Level Design owns arena space and safe routes.\nSmall-enemy releases and interactive valves are proposed mechanics, not narrative requirements.\n\nSuggested exit: return toward a service access/exit after the revelation, then a brief dispatch transition.\nDo not require entering the portal or choose a second-level destination yet. Keep the support plumber's location\nconsistent; a radio reply must not imply they suddenly stand beside the selected hero.\n\n## Dialogue sources and implementation boundaries\n\nThe current approved opening and route-specific prototype endings live in\n[story_dialogue.gd](../scripts/story_dialogue.gd). Use that source for exact text and semantic portrait emotions.\n\n- Opening plays after selection on a fresh new game; either choice uses the same introduction.\n- Do not replay the opening on death, checkpoint recovery, or retry.\n- All conversations are skippable. Preserve gameplay freeze, device-appropriate prompts, and dismissal input guards.\n- Between-level conversations should generally run four to eight lines and reveal one meaningful development.\n- Both character routes convey the same essential facts through distinct dialogue.\n- Essential discoveries must not depend on optional radio remarks during combat.\n- Every line carries a semantic emotion. Tony's kindness is the default; skepticism is not contempt for Sean.\n\nThe current completion scripts describe clearing the prototype area and receiving another address. They do not\ndescribe a boss, repaired plumbing, or a portal. They are suitable only while those beats are absent. Once the boss\nand reveal are implemented, replace the completion scene with a dedicated scene rather than stacking contradictory\nendings. In particular, do not claim all enemies are gone if optional enemies can remain alive.\n\n## Proposed portal exchange, not final dialogue\n\nThis earlier Storyboarding sketch expresses the intended reveal and evasion. Adapt it for selected/support roles\nand obtain a finalized script before treating it as production dialogue.\n\n> Sean: Tony... where does that pipe go?\n>\n> Tony: It shouldn't go anywhere. That's an outside wall.\n>\n> BJ: Your next assignment is ready.\n>\n> Tony: We've got something here you need to see.\n>\n> BJ: I have already seen everything necessary. Proceed to the exit.\n\nFor this exchange to work, establish Tony's sightline or a shared camera view when he is supporting remotely.\nOtherwise rewrite the observation. Do not silently grant the radio partner visual omniscience.\n\n## Remaining decisions\n\n- Final route and encounter plan, boss implementation scope, and exit placement.\n- Whether the portal reveal ships with the first full-length level or is explicitly deferred.\n- Final character-specific boss/reveal dialogue once actual implemented events are known.\n- Source of the living fatberg, portal destination, and relationship to BJ's later corruption.\n- Second-level destination. Earlier locations remain candidates, not an agreed itinerary.\n\nLevel Design and Engineering own roadmap integration for this coordination. This brief makes no build, screenshot,\nor delivered gameplay claims.\n",
                    "truncated": false
                  }
                }
              ]
            },

            {
              "type": "userMessage",
              "id": "01a13c5b-75fb-7390-99b7-3685d356efed",
              "content": [
                {
                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "You know what? We should have some story/dialog between each level, shouldn't we? Something that pushes the plot along so the player can find out what's going on. What do you think?\n"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016acff6a9597c819abbc19560c45ea349",
              "text": "Yes—**each level should reveal something that changes how Tony and Sean understand the job.** A short conversation afterward can connect that discovery to their next assignment.\n\nI’d aim for **four to eight lines between levels**, always skippable. Each scene should do three things:\n\n- React to what the player just encountered.\n- Reveal one clue or develop the partnership.\n- Give a concrete reason to go to the next location.\n\nThe broader progression could work like this, without locking in the locations yet:\n\n| Story stage | What changes |\n|---|---|\n| **Opening assignment** | BJ describes a routine basement problem. Tony suspects he’s understating it. |\n| **After the Clogfather** | They discover the proposed portal. BJ hurriedly redirects them. This is bigger than a blockage. |\n| **Next investigation** | They find evidence that BJ’s decisions helped spread the trouble. He supplies an explanation that doesn’t quite fit. |\n| **Midpoint** | Tony and Sean deliberately investigate something BJ told them to ignore. Sean notices an important inconsistency. |\n| **Late game** | BJ starts issuing contradictory instructions. His mistakes become harder to distinguish from another presence interfering. |\n| **Before the finale** | The takeover becomes undeniable. Tony and Sean make their own plan, with both contributing. |\n\nWe should let the player **see the evidence during gameplay** before the characters discuss it: impossible pipework, altered shipping labels, growth inside a terminal. That makes the dialogue a payoff rather than a lecture.\n\nThe selectable-character idea gives these scenes extra value. Both playthroughs reveal the same essential facts, but through different exchanges. Tony might identify why a plumbing installation is impossible; Sean might ask why a supposedly abandoned facility received a delivery yesterday.\n\nAnd some scenes should be sincere. After a rough level, Tony checking whether Sean is okay can matter more than another BJ punchline. That gives the comedy—and their eventual trust—something to land against.\n\nMy recommendation: **one brief opening exchange, one discovery-driven conversation between levels, and a slightly longer finale.** Optional radio remarks can add personality during play without carrying essential plot information.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]

                "text": "# Global coding standards\n\nRead the sections relevant to the task before editing or reviewing that file type.
